Title: Machine Learning Techniques for Distinguishing Android Malware Variants
Author: Irwansyah, Irwansyah
Journal: Journal of Applied Data Sciences
Abstract: The advancement of portable devices has been quickly and dramatically reshaping the usage trend and consumer preferences of electronic devices. Android, the most common mobile operating system, has a privilege-separated protection system with a complex access control mechanism. Android apps require permission to get access to confidential personal data and device resources. However, studies have shown that various malicious applications can acquire permission and target systems and applications by misleading users. In this study, we suggest a machine-learning approach to classifying Android malware variants by mining requested permissions, real permissions, suspicious calls, and API calls that were obtained and used in Android malware applications. Selected features were selected using a feature selection called KBest. Feature selection techniques are used to minimize the scale of the features and increase the performance. Two types of Naïve Bayes classifiers, called Multinomial distribution and multivariate Bernoulli distribution, are used and compared in malware family classification for text classification. Both naïve Bayes types are evaluated using a confusion matrix based on 4022 Android malware applications belonging to 10 families. Experimental findings show that the Multinomial distribution offers a reliable performance from three tests experiment with an average accuracy of 95%. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Ideal Lattice-Based Efficient Data Sharing Scheme for Cloud Storage
Author: Li, Yanjun; Wu, Jinlong; Liu, Jian; Huo, Shanshan; Zhang, Yuzhu
Abstract: The proliferation of cloud computing has rendered secure data sharing a paramount challenge, particularly in the post-quantum era where quantum computers threaten traditional public-key cryptosystems. While many schemes exist, achieving fine-grained, efficient, and quantum-resistant access control remains a key research area. To this end, this paper proposes a post-quantum secure data sharing scheme based on ideal lattices. We construct a new Ciphertext Policy Attribute-Based Encryption (CP-ABE) scheme for key distribution over ideal lattices, integrated into a hybrid encryption mechanism to protect data privacy efficiently. This approach allows data owners to enforce complex access policies on their encrypted data, ensuring that only authorized users can access it. Rigorous security proofs demonstrate that the proposed scheme is IND-CPA-secure under the Ring-LWE assumption. The efficiency of the scheme is due to its effective utilization of the algebraic structure of the ideal lattice, which accelerates polynomial operations through Number Theoretic Transformations (NTT). Comparative analysis and experimental results show that the scheme has significant advantages in computing efficiency and storage cost, thereby underscoring its practical feasibility for high-throughput cloud environments.

Title: Security Issues and Weaknesses in Blockchain Cloud Infrastructure: A Review Article
Author: Albaroodi, Hala A
Journal: Journal of Applied Data Sciences
Abstract: Cloud computing has become an essential technology due to its ability to provide scalable infrastructure and data services at a low cost and with minimal effort. It is widely adopted across various IT sectors and excels in providing flexible and scalable solutions for storage, computation, and networking. However, despite its widespread adoption, information security concerns remain a significant challenge, hampering its full potential. Issues such as data breaches, insufficient access controls, privacy risks, and vulnerability to external attacks persist, making security a critical obstacle for cloud computing’s growth. At the same time, blockchain technology has emerged as a promising solution for addressing these security challenges. Celebrated for ensuring data integrity, authenticity, and confidentiality, blockchain’s decentralized structure offers a potential safeguard against the risks cloud systems face. For instance, blockchain’s ability to maintain an immutable, tamper-proof ledger and decentralized control can mitigate unauthorised access risks, thereby enhancing cloud environments' transparency and security. One of the blockchain’s core components is the consensus protocol, a method through which a network of nodes validates transactions without needing to trust any single entity. In the case of Bitcoin, users follow the Proof of Work algorithm, dedicating hardware and energy resources to solve cryptographic puzzles and verify transactions. This decentralized verification process addresses fraud concerns, but it also brings challenges such as high energy consumption and network centralization, particularly in regions with cheap electricity. These concerns have led to worries about collusion risks and policy changes affecting the stability of the network. Blockchain’s decentralized nature has sparked significant interest, especially in its potential to enhance cloud computing security. Its ability to provide tamper-proof transaction logs, eliminate single points of failure, and grant users more control over data aligns well with the security demands of cloud environments. However, blockchain itself faces challenges, including scalability issues and its association with black-market trading due to its open-access model. Despite these concerns, blockchain’s integration into cloud systems presents a unique opportunity for addressing key security obstacles, thereby offering more robust solutions for corporate and financial applications. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Information security risks associated with the uncontrolled storage of secrets in source code
Author: Chornii, V.; Martseniuk, Y.; Partyka, A.; Harasymchuk, O.
Abstract: This paper explores the problem of information security violations caused by the uncontrolled storage of sensitive data in software source code. Specifically, it analyzes cases involving the inclusion of API keys, access tokens, database passwords, cloud platform credentials, and other confidential data in public or private repositories, which pose significant threats to the integrity of IT infrastructures. The research involves an empirical analysis of open-source repositories on GitHub using specialized secret detection tools such as TruffleHog, GitLeaks, and detect-secrets. The collected data were classified according to the types of discovered objects, allowing for the identification of the most common risk vectors. Special emphasis is placed on infrastructure-related threats that arise from storing secrets in CI/CD pipelines, configuration files, and automated deployment scripts. The study proposes approaches for integrating secret management into the software development lifecycle (SDLC), including automated scanning, centralized credential management, and the implementation of role-based access policies. Furthermore, a risk assessment based on the NIST SP 800-30 methodology was conducted to demonstrate the severity of potential secret leaks and to substantiate the need for secure DevSecOps processes. The paper presents practical recommendations for risk mitigation, including key rotation, personnel training, enforcement of role-based access control mechanisms, and periodic audits of development environments. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Strengthening Cloud Security with ECSM-QKDP: A Quantum Key Distribution Protocol Approach
Author: Anumula, Sathish Krishna
Abstract: The research delivers an advanced version of Cloud Security Model defined as ECSM-QKDP which implements quantum cryptographic methods to protect cloud data. The proven quantum key distribution (QKD) method BB84 runs as an integral part in the model to perform secure key transfers between cloud entities. Data encryption through Hierarchical Attribute-Set Based Encryption (HASBE) delivers increased security and manages access control procedures. The implementation executes quantum cryptographic simulations through CloudSim Qiskit and iQuantum which operate in the cloud environment. The paper conducts experimental assessments to test ECSM-QKDP against AKE and PDP security protocols as well as other encryption models in the market. The results demonstrate key computation time decreases by 39.9% and encryption and decryption operations operate at 78% faster speed and cloud memory utilization reaches 55% better efficiency against standard security methods. The model ensures 99.8% secure cloud service delivery because it stands up well against quantum threats. The addition of distance bounding techniques in the developed Secure Authentication Protocol (SAP) enhances overall security features. ECSM-QKDP proves itself as a viable method to protect cloud-based data through efficient quantum security protocols which demonstrate scalability and quantum security.

Title: Zero-Trust Evolution and Cloud Computing Security as Multi-Mission Engineering: Addressing Emerging Threats, Regulations, and Modeling Solutions via Enhancing Blockchain Consensus Algorithm to Mitigate Data Repository Breaches
Author: Singh, B.; Kaunert, C.
Abstract: The convergence of Zero Trust Evolution and Cloud Computing Security reflects a paradigm shift from traditional security models. Recognizing the limitations of perimeter-based defense mechanisms, this research delves into the concept of Zero Trust, which emphasizes continuous verification and dynamic risk assessment of users and devices, regardless of their location within a network. This proactive approach aims to ensure data protection and access control in an environment where threats are becoming increasingly sophisticated and pervasive. The concept of “Multi-Mission Engineering” emphasizes the need for a multifaceted strategy to tackle diverse cyber threats. This strategy recognizes that security challenges extend beyond a single approach and advocates for an integrated approach that combines Zero Trust principles with Cloud Computing Security strategies. By doing so, the research acknowledges that security is not a one-size-fits-all endeavor, but rather a dynamic and adaptive endeavor that encompasses multiple layers of protection. To enhance security through the integration of a Blockchain Consensus Algorithm, known for its immutability and decentralized nature, it is introduced as a means to mitigate data repository breaches. By leveraging a robust consensus algorithm, data integrity can be ensured, unauthorized access can be curtailed, and data breaches can be minimized. Throughout the research, case studies, simulations, and real-world scenarios are employed to illustrate the practical implications of this integrated approach. By evaluating the potential risks, benefits, and challenges associated with the proposed solution, the research provides a comprehensive assessment of the viability of the approach in a dynamic and evolving cyber landscape. The research paper encapsulates the fusion of Zero Trust Evolution, Cloud Computing Security, and Blockchain technology as a multi-mission engineering strategy to address emerging cyber threats and enhance data security. By embracing innovation and a multi-faceted approach, the research seeks to contribute to the ongoing dialogue surrounding the evolution of cybersecurity paradigms and the utilization of cutting-edge technologies to safeguard critical digital assets. The paper begins by elucidating the foundational principles of Zero Trust, emphasizing its shift from perimeter-centric security to continuous verification and adaptive risk management. Cloud Computing Security’s pivotal role in the digital ecosystem is explored, highlighting the impor tance of safeguarding data in cloud environments. With a comprehensive review of emerging threats such as data breaches, identity theft, and insider attacks, the paper underscores the need for innovative solutions. It proposes a novel approach that combines Zero Trust and Cloud Computing Security, advocating for an integrated defense-in-depth strategy that fosters resilience against evolving threats. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: CenterYou++: Lightweight Privacy Enforcement for Android Using Hybrid AI and Cloud Decision Support
Author: Safavi, Seyedmostafa; Shukur, Zarina; Rana, Muhammad Ehsan
Abstract: While the Android operating system provides a vast application ecosystem offering extensive functionalities, it concurrently introduces substantial challenges to preserving user privacy. Mobile applications frequently engage in widespread collection of personal data, and users often encounter difficulties in managing application permissions effectively, creating exposure to potential privacy infringements. Existing techniques for privacy enforcement frequently encounter difficulties in achieving an optimal balance among scalability, user-centric design principles, and the critical need for timely responsiveness. To overcome these limitations, this work introduces CenterYou++, a novel privacy enforcement framework engineered specifically for Android environments. This framework employs a hybrid architecture, distinctively merging the capabilities of lightweight, on-device artificial intelligence (AI) agents with the resources of cloud-based decision support. The on-device AI facilitates low-latency, localized privacy enforcement actions grounded in learned behavioral patterns and predefined rules. Concurrently, the cloud component furnishes access to current privacy policies and global threat intelligence, while also underpinning the system's scalability. This synergistic design yields considerable advantages, encompassing real-time privacy enforcement capabilities, a more intuitive user experience achieved through automation and transparency, and strengthened policy enforcement mechanisms. The overarching objective is to establish an equilibrium between robust privacy protection and a fluid, unobtrusive user experience.

Title: ResQlink: An Emergency Response WebApp
Author: T, Keerthika; Shijish, Arya Palackal; A, Kritika; S, Meenakshy; Rajeev, Riya
Abstract: ResQlink Emergency Response WebApp is a web-based platform that is designed for emergency reporting, response coordination, and user management. While technologies like two-way communication, dynamic tracking, ML-based hazard detection, and AI agents have been implemented there are limitations.This frontend is built with the help of React with TypeScript and Material-UI for UI components, while the backend uses Flask with MongoDB for data storage. This entire model helps in secure authentication with the help of JWT and bcrypt, that gives surety on role-based access for users, responders, and admins. RESTful APIs eases smooth communication between frontend and backend, while NLP (NLTK) helps in text classification for prioritizing emergencies. Geolocation services like OpenStreetMap and Nominatim are included for accurate location tracking. The platform makes sure that theres data security, real-time updates, and efficient emergency handling, making it a good system for crisis management.

Title: Enhancing Data Secure CSP Framework for User Authorization using Hybrid(Kyber-AES) Algorithm with HGA-MPSOA Optimization Algorithm in Banking Transactions
Author: Yuvarani, R.; Mahaveerakannan, R.
Abstract: This paper presents a novel Hybrid Cloud Security Framework designed to enhance user authorization and data protection in banking transactions by integrating Kyber, a postquantum secure key encapsulation mechanism, with AES-256 symmetric encryption. To address the challenges of quantum threats, inefficient key management, and computational overhead in cloud security, the proposed system employs a hybrid cryptographic model combining the quantum resistance of Kyber with the high-speed encryption capabilities of AES. Additionally, the framework incorporates a Hybrid Genetic Algorithm with Modified Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm (HGA-MPSOA) to dynamically optimize encryption parameters, thereby reducing processing latency and computational complexity. The system architecture features a three-layered approach—User, Cloud Service Provider, and Data Layers—that collectively ensure secure credential handling, transaction processing, dynamic key management, and audit-enabled fraud detection. Experimental analysis demonstrates that this integrated approach achieves robust security, improved performance, and scalability suitable for real-time banking operations and largescale IoT-cloud ecosystems. The framework offers a promising direction for future-proof cloud security solutions in the financial sector.

Title: Adaptive Trust Management in Dynamic Multi-Cloud Environments using Performance Specifications and Real-Time Policy Matching
Author: Gupta, Indrajeet; Kumar, Rakesh Ranjan; Muduli, Debendra; Panda, Risheeta
Abstract: With the rising popularity of multi-clouds, trust management has become essential to ensure secure and dependable service delivery. Existing trust models are not designed to handle the dynamic characteristics of multi-cloud systems, where fluctuating performance, varying SLAs, and emerging security risks significantly affect reliability. This work proposes an adaptive trust management framework that uses performance specifications (P-Specs) and a Policy Matching Engine (PME) to evaluate trust in real time. P-Specs measures CSP performance using metrics like availability, latency, and data integrity, while PME performs live compliance checks to dynamically update trust levels. The proposed system supports anomaly detection and policy enforcement to mitigate security threats and optimize decision-making. Experimental results using a simulated multicloud environment demonstrate enhanced accuracy, responsiveness, and policy compliance. This paper presents a robust and scalable trust management solution to improve security and reliability in heterogeneous dynamic infrastructures.

Title: Advanced Encryption Techniques for Enhancing Data Security and Privacy in Cloud Environments
Author: Shah, Parth; Shah, Samarth; Agrawal, Anurag
Abstract: This paper presents a novel hybridised encryption framework, BH-WABE, for securing cloud data, which combines symmetric encryption (Blowfish) and attribute-based encryption (ABE) to ensure fine-grained access control. The proposed scheme utilises a weight attribute-based authority (WAA) to dynamically assign attribute weights, enforcing hierarchical access policies and ensuring multi-authority security and resistance to collusion. Performance evaluations show that the encryption time increases from 118 ms to 341 ms, and the decryption time rises from 113 ms to 598 ms as the file size grows from 1 MB to 3 MB, with throughput remaining stable at approximately 0.00847 to 0.00874. Comparative analysis with the base E-ART algorithm reveals that BH-WABE outperforms E-ART in both encryption and decryption times. For instance, BH-WABE achieves encryption times of $\mathbf{1 1 8 ~ s, 2 3 0}$ s, and 341 s for file sizes of $1 \mathrm{MB}, 2 \mathrm{MB}$, and 3 MB, respectively, while E-ART lags behind with higher encryption times.

Title: Bypassing Third-Party Login Platform Authentication for Mobile Apps
Author: Zhang, Xiaoqi; Huang, Yuhang; Wang, Jice; Zhou, Yangfan; He, Fannv; Wu, Gaofei; Zhang, Yuqing
Abstract: Third-party authorization simplifies the registration and login process for new applications or websites by allowing users to utilize their existing third-party accounts. Third-party platforms have integrated their own login functionality code into SDK for developers to use. However, these SDKs, if poorly designed, can lead to security issues. Attackers may exploit available information in conjunction with design flaws in the SDKs to launch attacks, posing a significant threat to user privacy. The paper further investigates the security of OAuth services in SDKs, building on previous attack methods. Our experiments show that, despite updates to app hardening techniques, these attacks remain effective, highlighting the limitations of current defenses. The attack we mentioned enables successful account hijacking, which we demonstrated using Weibo as a case study. To understand the scope of this attack, we evaluated the top 1000 apps by download volume in the Xiaomi app store and found that 26% of these apps are vulnerable to our attack. Subsequently, we explored the potential hazards of this model and combining existing issues with defensive strategies, further refined preventive measures against such threats. Based on this phenomenon, we have conducted further research into the security of OAuth services as implemented within SDK, proposing a new threat model for third-party logins via web authorization.

Title: Why Perimeter Security is No Longer Enough: Observations and Open Challenges
Author: Ojha, N.; Vaish, A.
Abstract: Trust is the most important factor, which was a critical deciding factor in all security measures of traditional perimeter security models. However, the dynamic nature of attacks has changed the scenario drastically, where these models failed to address the failures. VPNs, firewalls, DMZs, and other identity-based access models—all security controls—were a good fit for protecting contemporary legacy devices and classical models. However, evolving AI and generative models of AI have pushed these security models to their limitations. In this book chapter, the limitations of these legacy devices have been discussed. A comparative analysis of all devices, comprising VPN, firewall, IAM, DMZ, and so forth, has been conducted, focusing on their demerit cases considering trust as a factor, inside or outside. This chapter has also examined how the advancement of cloud computing, hybrid networks, and complex IT environments, including mobile frameworks, is giving rise to a situation in which the existing model is inadequate. Additionally, it has explored how the zero-trust security framework can offer its assistance in this context. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: AI-SECURED VISITOR MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
Author: Reddy, J.B.; Sagar, R.; Lahari, L.; Namitha, N.; Murthy, N.N.; Pillai, N.N.
Abstract: In general, there are so many organizations using the conventional paper log book to record the access of the visitors. This conventional method takes longer time if the number of visitors exceeds the limit. Meanwhile, security issue should be a main concern if there is an increase in the number of visi tors. This is mainly due to the operators who take a long time to verify the identification of each and every visitor when there is huge number of visi tors entering the premises. Moreover, paper log is inadequate to efficiently retrieve and archive the data after several years. This report mainly discusses about the design and implementation of Visitor Management System using Internet of Things (IoT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI). Visitor management system is a security system which is used to track visitor’s activities in an organization or public building. ESP32 AI Thinker is used to collect the live stream video. Face detection and identification of visitor’s can be achieved through Artificial Intelligence (AI). With the help of IoT, we can remote access the system for visitor monitoring. The visitor’s information gets stored into a cloud server which helps the user to view the visitor’s details on mobile phone at any time. With the help of an API, the user can control the access of a visitor into the premises through notification alerts. A website has been created in order to store the details of visitor’s such as photograph, arrival time with the help of dijango web application frame work and bootstrap for user interface. DigitalOcean is the cloud server which is used to store the database. To get the notifications on mobile phone, a Telegram BoT API has been created in Telegram app. This BoT also saves the arrival time and photo of the visitor. With the help of this, the user will also be notified whenever a suspicious activity occurs in the premises. This IoT networked contact less security system offers improved security. AI secured Visitor Management System is the best solution to overcome the problems existing in the conventional method as it is the easy way to identify and record the information of a visitor. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Deployment of a Machine Learning-SDN Pipeline for IoT Threat Detection in Smart City Environments
Author: Rodrigues, Antonio Wendell De O.; Freitas, Francisco Erialdo D.; Rodrigues, Rejane Cavalcante Sá; Filho, Rogério Guerra Diógenes; De Araújo, André Luiz C.
Abstract: Smart cities rely on IoT systems that require adaptive security against evolving cyber threats. This paper presents a modular architecture combining machine learning (ML) with Software-Defined Networking (SDN) for real-time threat detection and mitigation in MQTT-based LoRaWAN networks. The system uses flow-level features to preserve privacy and enables dynamic policy enforcement via a REST API in the SDN control loop. We evaluate 13 ML models on the UNSW-NB15 dataset, with XGBoost achieving 0.8995 accuracy and 0.9927 AUC. Though based on synthetic data, the solution supports extensibility, SDN portability, and future integration of online and federated learning. Deployment feasibility, performance impact, and scalability are also addressed.

Title: Proceedings of International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Networks, ICAIN 2024, Volume 1
Author: Mishra, Ritu; Goyal, Sandip Kumar; Rana, Sanjeev
Abstract: Cloud computing is becoming increasingly necessary as time goes on. The main worry is the security of cloud computing. Data security becomes a critical problem since data stored in the cloud needs to be transferred via the internet. Integrity, confidentiality, accountability, privacy, access control, authentication, and authorization are crucial data protection procedures that must be upheld. By solving its security problems, blockchain technology improves cloud computing. Blockchain technology is a distributed ledger where data are shared among various network nodes, containing transaction specifics. Consensus techniques confirm transactions, ensuring immutability once data is recorded. The required technology is Bit coin, (digital Crypto currency). Instead of using a local server or a personal computer, the method of managing, storing, and processing data in the cloud network of remote computers housed on the internet. In this post, we’ve highlighted key challenges facing the cloud and proposed solutions through the integration of blockchain technology. To underscore their effectiveness, we’ll review previous research focused on combining blockchain with cloud technology.
Series: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems

Title: Optimizing Cloud Threat Detection with RCF, SVDD, CASB, and HBOS in Privacy-Centric Architectures
Author: Musham, Nagendra Kumar; Musam, Venkata Sivakumar; Jagathpally, Abhignya; Shahwar, Tayyaba; Mekala, R
Abstract: The explosive growth of cloud computing poses serious security concerns that require advanced threat detection systems. Traditional approaches are often lacking in scalability and privacy compliance. New techniques in real-time cloud threat detection include Random Cut Forest (RCF), Support Vector Data Description (SVDD), Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB), and Histogram-Based Outlier Detection (HBOS). The methodology proposed includes RCF, SVDD, CASB, and HBOS into privacy-centric designs. Each of these methods understands data distribution analysis, policy enforcement, and anomaly detection. If considered in combination, the above techniques can develop accurate real-time threat identification results. Their results are then aggregated in an ensemble-based categorization to identify risks with reliability and scalability but with privacy standards. The paper integrates RCF, SVDD, CASB, and HBOS into a privacy-centric framework in an effort to enhance the cloud environment through threat detection. Beyond the reduction in the cost of computation and the surety of data privacy, it has the eventual aim toward real-time detection of anomalies and establishment of an effective, scalable security solution for dynamic cloud environments. The integrated model surpassed the other more traditional methods such as PSO and HVMI in accuracy, precision, and F1-score (96.5%, 95%, and 94.8%, respectively). Due to its competitive computation time of 20 ms, it is ideal for real-time applications. For scalability and privacy maintenance in dynamic cloud environments, the proposed architecture was better compared to others. The hybrid model proposed will improve accuracy, real-time capability, and compliance with privacy while resolving cloud security issues. It will outperform the conventional techniques as it uses cutting-edge techniques that improve performance. This promotes safe and private designs by ensuring the detection of threats strongly for dynamic cloud environments.

Title: Hybrid Intelligent Systems, 23rd International Conference on Hybrid Intelligent Systems (HIS 2023), December 11-13, 2023, Volume 1: Healthcare Applications
Author: Kumar, Kishore; Kumar, G. Pavan; Sailaja, Y.; Senthil, P.; Kumar, Sheo; Syamsundar, C.
Abstract: The management and upkeep of health records have a significant influence on the effectiveness of healthcare services. Data privacy and security are of utmost importance in the field of medical services. Ensuring data security and secure storage of medical data are key concerns for the majority of individuals. The implementation of a technological platform is crucial in establishing a robust and reliable communication system inside a Healthcare System, ensuring both security and seamless functionality. The technology known as blockchain has undergone significant advancements during the past several years. The primary attributes of Blockchain that attract a significant number of developers include its Distributed Ledger, Decentralization, and Immutability. Hence, the utilization of Blockchain Technology presents a viable solution for securely storing personal medical data. The impact of its utilization in healthcare systems will be substantial. In recent times, there has been a notable change in the manner in which Health Records are stored in Mobile Cloud Environments. This change involves the integration of mobile devices with Cloud Computing, which enables the seamless interchange of medical data between Patients and Providers. The Healthcare system facilitates the provision of healthcare services at reduced operational expenses, while offering considerable adaptability and extensive access to medical data records. The system under consideration encompasses a framework for sharing Medical History, which integrates the use of Blockchain technology into a Desktop Application. Specifically, we have developed a reliable access control mechanism that ensures the secure sharing of health records among diverse individuals and healthcare professionals. In this study, we introduce a prototype implementation that utilizes machine learning techniques to forecast the appropriate disease diagnosis and therapy recommendation for patients based on their reported symptoms. Within this particular system, the utilization of a model facilitates the expeditious examination of patients’ symptoms by medical professionals, enabling them to promptly make informed decisions. Therefore, a machine learning model utilizes patient data to generate informed predictions, so aiding in the process of prescribing appropriate treatments.

Title: Microservices Architecture for Building a Crypto Freelance Exchange
Author: Popereshniak, S.; Bielikov, M.; Bur, A.
Abstract: The growth of freelancing exposed several drawbacks in the platforms that are now in use, including high service costs, fraud risks, and late payments [1]. A well-designed system architecture is necessary to develop a freelance platform to guarantee scalability, security, and effectiveness. A modular architecture was chosen to give the required flexibility, scalability, and ease of maintenance to overcome these issues. This paper presents the design of a microservices-based architecture for a crypto freelance exchange platform, which uses Domain-Driven Design principles [2]. The architecture is built to support decentralized transactions, smart contract integration, and secure user authentication. It also ensures high availability and fault tolerance. The system uses a multi-layered architecture incorporating PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, and Web3.js. The main components are a web application, KrakenD API Gateway, auth microservice, files microservice, and main microservice for managing transactions, orders, and payments. They are designed to meet critical non-functional requirements such as scalability, security, and maintainability. Each service can be independently deployed, updated, and scaled according to transaction volumes. With an emphasis on security, the platform uses JWT token techniques and multi-factor authentication to authenticate users. Also, the integration of blockchain technology enhances transparency, enabling freelancers and clients to have a trusted record of all transactions and reducing the risk of fraud. The architecture is visualized through UML and C4 model diagrams showing component interactions and service orchestration. This paper also discusses the rationale behind the chosen technologies, security mechanisms, and the benefits of using a modular microservices approach for building a crypto freelance platform. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Tailoring AI and Cloud in Modern Enterprises to Enhance Enterprise Architecture Governance and Compliance
Author: Kabade, Satish; Sharma, Akshay; Chaudhari, Bhushan Balkrishna
Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and cloud computing technology implementation in modern enterprises helps them operate more flexibly and scalable with optimum results on the efficiency scales. The integration of these technologies into the Enterprise Architecture (EA) causes governance and compliance management as well as risk management problems. The research uses Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning (MADRL) to optimize cloud infrastructure operations by fulfilling both enterprise governance standards and industry regulations. The developed intelligent system learns to generate optimal outcomes, which simultaneously produce the highest compliance benefits with minimum operational expenses and upper-level performance improvement through multiple decision sequences. System metric collection starts the methodology, which is then followed by training a (MADRL) model for effective resource management and governance policy enforcement. An intelligent system supports adherence to security regulations, efficient workloads and compliance by rewarding good behavior, but punishes those who do not comply or whose results are ineffective. During its 100 training sessions, the model develops its decision-making capabilities, and assessment happens by evaluating its response times and efficiency costs while analyzing reward values. The study verifies MADRL’s possibility to automate cloud operations while enhancing regulatory compliance as well as operational performance.

Title: Outsourced Verifiable Privacy-preserving Federated Learning via Sensitive Samples
Author: Han, Xu; Tang, Xiangyun; Weng, Yu; Gao, Yutong; Liu, Xuan
Abstract: Federated Learning (FL) based on Differential Privacy (DP) has become a popular method to enhance data privacy by protecting client data contributions during training. However, existing solutions typically assume a uniform privacy budget for all records, providing one-size-fits-all solutions that may fail to meet the diverse privacy requirements of individual records. Furthermore, FL vulnerable to model integrity attacks when resource-constrained users outsource training processes to cloud services. In this paper, We propose OVeriFL, an outsourced verifiable privacy-preserving FL scheme that integrates Personalized Differential Privacy (PDP) for adaptive privacy protection and uses sensitive samples for model integrity verification. Specifically, we define sensitive samples as a set of imperceptibly transformed inputs that are highly sensitive to model parameter changes. Even minor modifications to the model can be clearly reflected in the model outputs. Experimental results show that OVeriFL not only reliably detects model integrity attacks in cloud-hosted environments but also improves model utility by mitigating catastrophic forgetting and reducing accumulated noise through its PDP mechanism with the Poisson sampling procedure.

Title: Research on the Application of Cloud Desktop Technology in Constructing Collaborative Office Environment for Enterprise External Personnel
Author: Li, Bo; Li, Qian; Yu, Shasha; Feng, Yiqian; Hao, Zuyi
Abstract: This paper aims at the problems such as chaotic management of external personnel's devices and high risks of intellectual property leakage in the enterprise internal network, and proposes to construct a virtualized cloud desktop collaborative office environment that is completely isolated from both the enterprise internal network and the Internet. The designed collaborative office environment solution includes a dedicated network architecture, resource management, customized desktop services, and enhanced security protection. By using virtualization technology to achieve pooling and dynamic allocation of computing resources, and combining security mechanisms such as access control, data encryption, and watermark traceability, it ensures that external personnel can carry out collaborative office work in the enterprise internal network while strengthening security control, keeping intellectual property rights within the enterprise. The research results provide a safe and efficient technical path for the management of external personnel in the enterprise internal network environment, and are of great significance for safeguarding the security of enterprise data assets and improving operational efficiency.

Title: Integrating Google Cloud Identity and Access Management (IAM) with Managed File Transfer for Data Protection
Author: Chellu, Raghava
Abstract: Encryption is critical when transferring files to and from the Cloud storage platforms, and this calls for use of optimized and secure transfer means. This paper will therefore seek to examine the possibilities of applying Google Cloud IAM in connection with the IBM Sterling File Gateway, part denying managed file transfer (MFT) security. It provides other non-critical options such as MFA, and RBAC, and encryption as its crucial options. The paper also discusses certain significant concepts like regulation which include GDPR as well as HIPAA. It also explains various challenges when it comes to the integration of IAM-MFT and possible solutions like using AI security policies and the zero-trust models. This is the implication that IAM integration has the capability of increasing access control and strengthening the security of Cloud data. In the paper, it is proposed to integrate MFT systems with Google Cloud IAM, which allows for making data more secure by applying central access control, RBAC, and MFA. Policy based encryption and automated compliance audit along with the standardized IAM MFT templates are the solutions. Hardware accelerated encryption plus self-service IAM reduce the challenges of performance overhead. In the second part, the security aspects using the A1Driven models for threat detection and zero trust enforcement in the hybrid Cloud is explored.

Title: Electronic Healthcare Data Sharing Application Based on Hyperledger Consortium Blockchain Network
Author: Gupta, Ajay Kumar; Raj, Dharm; Sharma, Yogesh Kumar; Sharma, Akansha; Singh, Murari Kumar; Agrawal, Amrit Kumar
Abstract: The fragmentation of medical data, lack of patient ownership over medical records, and the persistent risk of data breaches represent significant challenges in the electronic healthcare sector. This research leverages blockchain technology and decentralized principles to address these issues by proposing a novel medical data-sharing system and business network model, with patient-owned medical records as the central asset. The proposed model ensures that ownership of medical records is unequivocally assigned to patients, granting them sole authority to authorize access to their personal health information. Furthermore, the system guarantees the immutability and chronological integrity of medical records. To realize this model, we implement a consortium blockchain network utilizing the Hyperledger Fabric framework, complemented by the Hyperledger Composer toolset for constructing the business network. The interstellar File System (IPFS) serves as a distributed storage solution, while the Angular framework facilitates the development of interactive web applications. Advanced technologies, including Docker, are employed to seamlessly integrate technical and business components, culminating in a fully functional blockchain-based application for medical data sharing. This application, accessible via web interfaces, empowers patients with control over their data, enhances security, and fosters a tamper-proof, interoperable healthcare ecosystem. Our findings demonstrate the potential of Hyperledger Fabric-based solutions to revolutionize data management in electronic healthcare, offering a scalable and patient-centric approach to medical record stewardship.

Title: ADDRESSING SECURITY CHALLENGES IN DECENTRALIZED ACCESS CONTROL: A BLOCKCHAIN AND ADAPTIVE LEARNING PERSPECTIVE
Author: Thingom, C.; Christiana, M.B.V.; Balaji, K.; Ravi, T.; Gopal, S.B.; Muni, T.V.; Thilagavathy, A.; Augustine, P.J. John; Sashmi, S.N.; Vidhya, R.G.
Journal: Journal of Theoretical and Applied Information Technology
Abstract: The Blockchain is also quickly becoming a disruptive technology for providing people with never-before-seen self-governance by virtue of it being secure, transparent, and decentralized in nature. Due to its nature, it has also come to form the basis for various industry applications apart from serving as an early impetus for next-generation paradigms like cloud as well as edge computing. For security concerns data-sharing applications with distributed access control, the current work proposes a new disruptive approach as an adaptive learning model for addressing the above security concerns. Python programming is also implemented for the system validation. A comparison is also made between ALM of the new proposed work with available encrypting algorithms like RSA and AES. Various parameters are also quantified by the research work, and data thus fed is tabulated in fine details. The result demonstrates enhanced security, scalability, as well as computational efficiency by the proposed algorithm. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Smart Care System with Dual-Model Cooperative Triggering for Anomaly Detection
Author: Xu, Feng-Yu; Pan, Yu-Jen; Lee, Jen-Chun; Cheng, Rung-Shiang
Abstract: This paper introduces an intelligent monitoring system designed for the timely detection of abnormal postures in elderly residents within care facilities. The system integrates deep learning-based posture detection, utilizing YOLOv10n, with facial recognition, employing a synergy of YOLOv10n-face and VGGFace2, to ensure accurate resident identification. A novel event-triggering mechanism, predicated on dual bounding box overlap, activates when the abnormal posture bounding box fully encapsulates the facial bounding box, achieving an Intersection over Union (IoU) of 1. Upon triggering, the system logs the event and its duration, storing the data in a backend database. If the abnormal posture persists beyond a pre-defined temporal threshold, immediate alerts are dispatched to caregivers via the LINE API. Authorized personnel can access real-time RTSP video streams and anomaly logs of assigned residents through a role-based access control (RBAC) web platform. The proposed system demonstrates high accuracy and responsiveness, indicating its significant potential for practical deployment in smart healthcare environments.

Title: CloudShare: A Passwordless Cloud-Based File Storage and Sharing Framework
Author: Kumar, K Dinesh; K, Niranjan D; Reddy, P Praneeth; Himanshu, P; Raju, K Sai; Goud, Praneeth
Abstract: Cloud-based file storage and sharing systems are widely used for collaborative work, data accessibility, and secure information dissemination. Traditional solutions often rely on password-based authentication, which introduces vulnerabilities such as credential theft, reuse attacks, and usability challenges. This paper presents CloudShare, a passwordless cloud-based file storage and sharing framework that enhances both security and user experience. CloudShare utilizes a challenge-response authentication protocol with asymmetric cryptography, eliminating the need for passwords while maintaining strong identity assurance. Users can upload, download, and securely share files with others, while file access is enforced through cryptographic ownership and explicit sharing permissions. The framework also introduces time-based access control mechanisms, enabling users to restrict file availability to specific time windows. The system is implemented using a web-based frontend and serverless backend architecture, offering scalability, ease of use, and end-to-end file confidentiality. CloudShare provides a practical and more secure alternative to traditional file sharing systems, particularly for environments where passwordless, controlled, and verifiable access is essential.
Series: 2025 International Conference on Computing Technologies (ICOCT)

Title: An Integration of Proxy Servers with Machine Learning for Imporving Security to Networks in Campus Wireless Network Systems
Author: Dhore, Prof M.L; Phand, Swaraj; Petkar, Parth; Patwardhan, Srujan
Abstract: Since educational institutions and organizations have relied on campus wide Wi-Fi, secure internet access has become more important with time. In this paper, we describe a proxy server-based system to monitor and control web access while using machine learning (ML) to predict potential cyber threats. Traffic is regulated by the system using a proxy server on a gateway machine, Squid. If a user asks to access a website, the proxy sees if the domain is on the blacklist. If it is, access is denied. If not, the request is then forwarded to an ML model trained on the UNSW-NB15 dataset to determine if there is a risk. The attack types in this dataset range from DoS, Worms, and Reconnaissance to give a complete coverage of threat detection. Machine learning component is comprised of Random Forest and XGBoost classifiers that have high recall rates to minimize the threats missed. With an admin dashboard, logs and traffic details are available for real time monitoring and decision making. The access control and predictive analytics are combined in this system to provide a scalable and reliable solution to network security. It integrates traditional proxy methods with cutting edge ML models for safe internet usage and protection users from evolving cyber threats in dynamically evolving network environments.

Title: Computational Science and Computational Intelligence, 11th International Conference, CSCI 2024, Las Vegas, NV, USA, December 11–13, 2024, Proceedings, Part VII
Author: Basudan, Sultan; Alamer, Abdulrahman; Qasim, Yunus Al
Abstract: Cloud computing is becoming increasingly common in the field of health care, in keeping with the rapid advancement of information technology. Sensing data utilization and confidentiality can be enhanced through the efficient and secure sharing of patient information. However, efficient forward secrecy is not supported by the cloud-based data sharing systems currently in use; if a data requester’s secret key is compromised, all previously provided data will be exposed. This paper presents an effective attribute-based data sharing scheme that provides flexible access control and guaranteed firm security over electronic health record (EHR) systems. In order to provide a shared secret key for data sharing that can be encrypted by an access structure over the data requester (DReq) characteristics, this technique combines attribute-based and puncturable encryption. Furthermore, the mutual authentication and shared key establishment are carried out concurrently by the cloud servers and DReqs. By utilizing the bloom filter approach, which effectively facilitates the updating of a secret key without requiring the key distributor to reissue the key, the suggested scheme can accomplish forward secrecy. This scheme complies with the security model, as demonstrated by the security proof. Additionally, the performance evaluation articulates the viability of the proposed plan.
Series: Communications in Computer and Information Science

Title: admin/1423: On the Insecurity of Open-Source 5G Core Network Deployments in the Wild
Author: Kohls, Katharina
Abstract: 5G promises improved performance and security features for our communication infrastructures, and cloud implementations of 5G core networks make private deployments more accessible. They accelerate the distribution of 5G-based communication networks for various use cases. However, the accessibility of a functional network implementation also bears the risk of maintaining a complex infrastructure with insecure configurations. In this work, we conduct a measurement study that focuses on selected interfaces of exposed core networks on the Internet. To this end, we scan for exposed management interfaces and analyze their security regarding insecure default login credentials, JWT tokens, exposed GTP ports, and cluster APIs. Our results indicate that a high number of deployed networks must be considered insecure.

Title: Blockchain in Health Sciences
Author: Kumar, Ashish; Gupta, Sachi; Sachdeva, Vrinda
Abstract: The implementation of Internet of Things (IoT) technology has resulted in a substantial and noteworthy transformation in healthcare systems. The use of IoT devices has enhanced the efficiency, convenience, and automation of health‐related services. Different IoT devices transmit vast quantities of captured data to the cloud, where it is processed to facilitate physicians’ access to information. In the case of cloud‐sensor architecture, where data transmission and reception incur significant latency, fog nodes are incorporated at the periphery of the sensor networks. However, due to the extremely sensitive nature of medical data, privacy, integrity, confidentiality, and access control are required. The aforementioned challenges may be resolved by employing blockchain technology, which can also foster trust between the healthcare service provider and the patient. This chapter thoroughly examines the integration of IoT technologies into the health sciences. Thereafter, it discusses the significance and difficulties associated with cloud‐based and fog‐based data storage and computation. It also covers the security aspects and difficulties associated with IoT technology‐based solutions, as well as the significance of blockchain in safeguarding medical data. Finally, it examines the future scope of this topic.
Series: Blockchain in Health Sciences

Title: A Comprehensive Survey on Secure Healthcare Data Management: Integrating Cloud Storage and AI-Driven Analytics
Author: Muthuvel, S; Kumar, K Sampath; Manoj, R Karthick
Abstract: The rapid digitization of healthcare systems has resulted in a significant increase in the quantity of sensitive patient data, requiring strong solutions for safe storage and sophisticated analytics. This work offers an in-depth examination of safe healthcare data management, emphasizing the use of cloud storage and AI-powered analytics. Cloud computing provides scalable and economical storage options; however, it also presents considerable security and privacy issues, especially for the management of sensitive health information. This work examines advanced encryption approaches, access control mechanisms, and data integrity methods intended to protect healthcare data in cloud settings. Furthermore, it investigates the function of AI-driven analytics in deriving actionable insights from extensive datasets, facilitating personalized medicine, predictive diagnoses, and enhanced patient outcomes. The intersection of AI and healthcare data prompts apprehensions over data integrity, prejudice, and ethical considerations. This assessment emphasizes upcoming concepts such federated learning, homomorphic encryption, and blockchain-based solutions, which seek to reconcile data usefulness with privacy protection. Additionally, it examines legislative frameworks such as GDPR and HIPAA and their influence on healthcare data management practices. This work seeks to provide a path for academics and practitioners by synthesizing recent accomplishments and pinpointing existing problems in the development of safe, efficient, and ethical healthcare data management systems. The amalgamation of cloud storage with AI-driven analytics has significant promise to transform healthcare; yet, it necessitates a multidisciplinary strategy to mitigate related risks and establish trustworthiness within the digital health ecosystem.

Title: ELWA Testbed-as-a-Service: An ECHONET Lite Web API Testbed with Heterogeneous IoT Devices
Author: Pham, Van Cu; Xin, Tao; Sioutis, Marios; Tan, Yasuo
Abstract: This paper presents a testbed for the ECHONET Lite Web API (ELWA), a protocol supporting cloud-to-cloud interoperability for IoT systems. The key innovation of the testbed lies in its ability to integrate IoT devices using any protocol or communication pattern through the introduction of an MQTT-based protocol binding and a token-based access management mechanism. This architecture enables a two-sided marketplace model, with the testbed server acting as a mediator between IoT device providers and service developers, realizing the testbed-as-a-service paradigm for the ELWA ecosystem. The proposed system has been implemented and deployed in a real-world environment with a variety of devices. Performance evaluations demonstrate the testbed’s scalability, reliably handling up to 3,000 concurrent requests per second, with minimal overhead introduced by protocol binding and access control mechanisms.

Title: Security Issues in Cloud Computing Using RSA Algorithm and Deployment Using Heroku
Author: Raj, Arman; Kumar, Avneesh; Johri, Prashant; Dheeraj
Abstract: Cloud Cloud Computing is one of the most emerging technologies and many industries, as well as consumers, are significantly shifting towards cloud servers for storing their data. However, there are a few security issues are there in the cloud and this requires little development to increase the efficiency and reliability of the Cloud. There are many sources such as address resolution protocol (ARP), IP spoofing, Botnets, Distributed Denial of Service attack (DDoS) etc where in different attacks can originate and plays a huge role in destroying sensitive data. It will completely describe how we can protect our crucial data by minimizing the risk and threats associated with this. Nowadays cloud computing is used by many organizations for storing their data, and the source of data comes from various places and a few weak data may corrupt other data. There is a need to understand the security issues and their challenges in this area. Security issues are one of the major concerns which have been affecting the growth of cloud technologies. In this paper, a comparative analysis is presented related to security and privacy techniques in cloud computing.

Title: AI-Driven Adaptive Gait Biometrics: Pioneering Real-Time Continuous Authentication for Enhanced Security
Author: Mekni, Mehdi; Ogunwobi, Emmanuel O.; Russell, Shannon C.; Nassar, Mohamad; Donyina, Adwoa
Abstract: Traditional authentication systems, reliant on single-checkpoint verification, remain vulnerable to post-authentication threats such as impersonation and session hijacking. This paper introduces a novel continuous authentication framework that leverages gait biometrics—a natural, spoof-resistant modality—enhanced by machine learning (ML) and real-time 3D skeletal data capture. Using a Microsoft Kinect sensor, kinematic features (e.g., stride length, joint angles) are extracted and processed via a Random Forest classifier to authenticate users dynamically. The system demonstrates 52.17% accuracy in controlled environments, though performance declines by 5% under suboptimal conditions (e.g., low lighting, obstacles). A modular microservices architecture ensures scalability, while encryption techniques and GDPR-compliant protocols preserve privacy. Challenges in heterogeneous environments underscore the need for multi-sensor fusion and deep learning integration. By balancing security and usability, this work advances gait biometrics as a passive, resilient solution for high-stakes applications such as secure access control, offering a critical step toward real-world deployment of continuous authentication systems.

Title: Port Forwarding Services Are Forwarding Security Risks
Author: Wang, Haoyuan; Xue, Yue; Feng, Xuan; Zhou, Chao; Mi, Xianghang
Abstract: We conduct the first comprehensive security study on two widely used port forwarding services (PFS), which emerge in recent years and make the web services deployed in internal networks available on the Internet along with better usability but less complexity compared to traditional techniques (e.g., NAT traversal techniques). Our study is made possible through a set of effective and efficient methodologies, which are designed to uncover the technical mechanisms of PFS, experiment attack scenarios for PFS protocols, automatically discover and snapshot port-forwarded websites (PFWs) at scale, and classify PFWs into well-observed categories. Leveraging these methodologies, we have observed the widespread adoption of PFS with millions of PFWs distributed across tens of thousands of ISPs worldwide. Furthermore, 32.31% PFWs have been classified into website categories that serve access to critical infrastructure or data, such as, web consoles for industrial control systems, IoT controllers, code repositories, and office automation systems. And 18.57% PFWs did not enforce any access control for external visitors. Also identified are two types of attacks inherent in the protocols of Oray (one well-adopted PFS provider), and the notable abuse of PFSes by malicious actors in activities such as malware distribution, botnet operation and phishing.

Title: Secure Deployment and Management of Applications Through Cloud-Based Automation
Author: M, Manjula; Grace, Joshila; Agarwal, Ankita; Gupta, Mohit; Panda, Aditi
Abstract: Cloud automation is a technology that provides the ability to rapidly deploy and manage applications in cloud environments. With the increasing popularity of cloud computing, organizations must be able to efficiently and securely deploy applications. The use of automation techniques in building the solution simplifies the entire Deployment and Onboarding at scale process, minimizing time & effort. Cloud technology provides auto-provisioning of resources; therefore, your apps scale automatically according to user demand. Furthermore, it also has enough high-level strong protection against potential threats such as cyber-attacks and data theft in prevention. Data encryption and access controls, along with regular security updates, ensure that sensitive data and applications are well-protected. This solution allows organizations to monitor the performance of their applications through these capabilities in real-time, thus making instant decisions to maintain service availability at all times.

Title: Innovations in Data Engineering: Sustainability for Societal and Industrial Impact, Proceedings of 5th International Conference on Data Engineering and Communication Technology (ICDECT 2024), Volume 1
Author: Turugare, Ranganai; Shava, Fungai Bhunu; Chitauro, Mercy
Abstract: The rapid growth of mobile health (mHealth) applications has revolutionized healthcare delivery, offering innovative solutions to address various healthcare challenges. However, this has raised concerns regarding the security and privacy of these applications, particularly those developed by solo or small team developers. This research paper analyzes mHealth apps for security vulnerabilities due to solo or small team development using the Open Web Application Security Project (OWASP)’s Top 10 vulnerabilities guidance and Quick Android Review Kit (QARK). By synthesizing insights from previous studies, the research highlights the critical importance of security in mHealth app development and the need for comprehensive security measures to protect user data and ensure the integrity of these applications. The analysis reveals that vulnerabilities in mHealth apps are primarily attributed to weak authentication and authorization, inadequate server-side control, lack of encryption, insecure communication, inadequate user input validation, and unprotected API usage. Future research will focus on strategies for enhancing the solo or small team developers’ security knowledge, resources availability, and supporting the integration of robust security practices throughout the development lifecycle to enhance the resilience of mHealth applications against cyber-threats and ensure the confidentiality and integrity of sensitive health data.
Series: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems

Title: Enhancing Cybersecurity and Secure Data Transmission in Cloud Computing Using Graph Neural Network Models
Author: Sharma, Seema; K, Vaishnavi; Shakir, Alakbarova Tamara; Lymareva, Ol’ga; Naidu, D J Samatha; S, Shankar
Abstract: Cloud computing has transformed data storage and administration, enabling users to access and save data online. Nonetheless, guaranteeing secure data transformation continues to be a significant cybersecurity concern, especially regarding the safe transmission of data within cloud systems. Conventional networks convey data via the most direct route between nodes, which may not ensure security. Customers encounter difficulties with cloud security and access control, notwithstanding the pay-as-you-go service model. The proposed system incorporates preprocessing and normalization modules to improve data security. Feature selection is enhanced through the utilization of GA, together with Mutation and Crossover procedures. GNN are utilized to efficiently depict dependencies between roles using graphical representations of neural networks. Experimental findings indicate the superiority of this method, with an average accuracy of 99.48% and an F1-score of 99.57% across all datasets. The performance research demonstrates that the GNN model much surpasses current security techniques, hence enhancing cybersecurity and facilitating secure data transformation. This study underscores the significance of sophisticated security frameworks in tackling emerging cloud security issues and accentuates the contribution of intelligent models in augmenting data protection.
Series: 2025 6th International Conference for Emerging Technology (INCET)

Title: Mind the Gaps: Toward a Unified Model of Multi-Cloud Firewall Configurations
Author: El-Shekeil, Ibrahim; Athamnah, Malek; Hounsinou, Sena G.
Abstract: Organizations are increasingly adopting multi-cloud strategies, leveraging the distinct capabilities provided by vendors such as Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP). Nonetheless, the unique methodologies of each platform for network access control present novel challenges in configuration, validation, and enforcement. Current studies on firewall rule misconfiguration generally presume a singular device or a single-cloud framework, neglecting the intricacies of multi-cloud settings. This study analyzes the disparity between conventional firewall assumptions and the contemporary diverse cloud environment. We demonstrate through practical examples how a configuration that is secure in one cloud can represent a vulnerability in another in a multi-cloud environment. We provide a systematic comparison of AWS, Azure, and GCP firewall architectures, emphasizing significant distinctions in rule semantics, assessment logic, and attachment points. We offer a cohesive architectural framework that standardizes providerspecific regulations, perpetually identifies deviations, and validates network access in accordance with planned standards. Our work aims to assist practitioners in managing intricate multicloud deployments with enhanced confidence and consistency by identifying the shortcomings of existing methodologies and delineating a strategy for scalable, cross-platform solutions.
Series: 2025 IEEE Cloud Summit

Title: Advances in Communication and Applications, Proceedings of ERCICA 2024, Volume 2
Author: Lokeshwari, R.; Kumar, M. Naveen; Jasmine, K. S.
Abstract: This paper presents the design, implementation, and evaluation of a secure file transfer management system built on the Linux platform. The system utilizes special group IDs to facilitate seamless communication between users while ensuring robust security measures. File manager is an API developed in Python, enabling efficient and reliable transfer of files from one user to another. The paper discusses the system's architecture, highlighting the integration of special group IDs for user authentication and access control. Key aspects of the development process include emphasizing the challenges and solutions encountered in leveraging Linux-specific features. Security considerations, including access control mechanisms, are thoroughly examined to ensure the confidentiality and integrity of transferred files. Overall, this paper provides valuable insights into implementing a secure and efficient file transfer management system on Linux, offering practical guidance for developers and administrators seeking to enhance user-to-user communication in their environments using GUI.

Title: Computational Science and Computational Intelligence, 11th International Conference, CSCI 2024, Las Vegas, NV, USA, December 11–13, 2024, Proceedings, Part VIII
Author: Chen, Louise Jia-Lu; Wu, Quincy; Wang, Jimmy
Abstract: Traditional firewalls apply the combination of source/destination IP addresses, port numbers, and protocols (UDP, TCP, or ICMP) to form access control lists (ACLs) which can effectively allow/deny traffic. However, with the rise of Cloud Data Centers like AWS and Akamai, ACLs face limitations in network management, especially with content delivery network (CDN) security challenges. This paper addresses the issues encountered by a powerful artificial intelligence assisted Juniper Mist Cloud management service. Mist Cloud requires the accessibility to AWS, which is usually prohibited by enterprise firewalls because of numerous unknown services on AWS. This paper proposes a solution with trusted third-party relay hosts for private enterprise networks. It details configurations for VPN Tunnel and firewall settings. Experimental results show minimal delay (only two milliseconds longer) when routing management traffic through a relay. This demonstrates that it provides a secure mechanism without sacrificing operations.
Series: Communications in Computer and Information Science

Title: Advancing Data Privacy in REST APIs: A Comparative Study of Machine Learning Techniques for PII Detection
Author: Sakapertana, Akbar Sahata; Faldi, Wan Muhafidz; Mahardika, Andi; Shiddiqi, Ary Mazharuddin
Abstract: The increasing use of REST APIs for data exchange has heightened the risk of exposing Personally Identifiable Information (PII), necessitating the development of automated detection systems to ensure software quality and compliance with regulatory standards. Global privacy regulations, including the GDPR and Indonesia's UU PDP, require organizations to effectively safeguard PII across various data formats, particularly unstructured data typically transmitted through APIs. Conventional approaches, such as rule-based detection, are inadequate for addressing the dynamic and semi-structured nature of API responses. This paper presents the application of machine learning techniques, specifically Support Vector Machines (SVM) and Naive Bayes classifiers, for detecting PII in REST API responses. The SVM model achieved an accuracy of 80.96%, a precision of 90.11%, a recall of 80.96%, and an F1-score of 84.37%, surpassing the performance of the Naive Bayes model. The results highlight the potential benefits of incorporating machine learning-based PII detection systems into the software development lifecycle to enhance API security, software quality, and compliance with privacy regulations.

Title: Advanced Strategies for Network Security: Ensuring Resilience in a Digital World
Author: Karimov, Majid M.; Karimova, Ikbola M.; Turdiyev, Temur T.
Abstract: The increasing sophistication of cyber threats necessitates a strategic approach to network security, ensuring resilience and safeguarding sensitive data. This paper explores contemporary methods of network security, focusing on preventive measures, detection strategies, and response mechanisms. Key areas of discussion include firewalls, intrusion detection systems, encryption techniques, and access control methodologies. Firewalls act as the first line of defense, filtering network traffic to prevent unauthorized access. Intrusion detection systems complement firewalls by monitoring and identifying potential threats in real time, leveraging machine learning for enhanced detection accuracy. Encryption techniques play a crucial role in data protection, employing symmetric, asymmetric, and hybrid encryption methods to maintain confidentiality and integrity. Additionally, authentication protocols such as multi-factor authentication and role-based access control ensure secure access management. The adoption of Zero Trust Architecture further enhances network security by requiring continuous verification of users and devices. Emerging trends, including artificial intelligence-driven threat detection and blockchain technology, offer promising advancements in cybersecurity frameworks. As organizations increasingly rely on cloud computing and the Internet of Things, the complexity of network security continues to evolve. Proactive measures, continuous monitoring, and adaptive security policies are essential in mitigating risks. By integrating innovative security strategies, businesses and individuals can establish a robust defense against cyber threats, ensuring a secure digital environment. This paper underscores the necessity of a comprehensive, multi-layered security approach to address the dynamic nature of cyber risks in today's interconnected world.

Title: Computational Intelligence in Machine Learning, Proceedings of the 3rd International Conference ICCIML 2023
Author: Reddy, G. Vinoda; Baig, Maughal Ahmed Ali; Unissa, Raheem; Babu, Ch. Raja Kishore; Sruthi, P.; Rao, K. Venkateswara
Abstract: Designing industrial systems that make use of digital technology is now possible thanks to the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT). Previously, this was not practical. The Industrial Internet of Things, sometimes known as RFID, is a crucial part of the IIoT. It enables industrial operators to identify things and link IoT time-series data with the recognized objects. Additionally, by using the cloud service, businesses might interchange data collected by IoT devices, facilitating information sharing and supporting them in making crucial production decisions. You could more effectively protect sensitive business affairs if there were a way to restrict who might see Internet of Things data stored in the cloud. For time-series IoT data, traditional cryptographic access control techniques have several issues concerning efficiency and key leakage. It is so since this kind of data was not intended to be used with conventional cryptographic access control systems. You are going to be expected to develop a secured industrial data access control system for the cloud-based Internet of Industrial Things (IIoT) as a component of this endeavor. Partners in the scheme are given the opportunity to restrict accessibility to their Internet of Things data in very specific ways using ciphertext-policy attribute-based encryption, or CP-ABE. The strategy makes use of a hybrid cloud infrastructure so that users may confidently trust the cloud service with time-consuming and resource-intensive CPABE chores without worrying about the security of their data. Importantly, the plan addresses the problem of key leakage by introducing an entirely novel form of data privacy for IoT devices, known as “item-level data protection.” Through the use of a number of various encryption and optimization techniques, you can achieve these goals. In order to ensure that the design is trustworthy and risk free, assessments of performance take into account both the system’s real functioning and in-depth computer modeling.

Title: Computational Intelligence in Machine Learning, Proceedings of the 3rd International Conference ICCIML 2023
Author: Kumar, Voruganti Naresh; Veerender, A.; Madhukar, G.; Soujanya, K. L. S.; Naryana, V. A.; Vivekananda, A.
Abstract: Since the Internet of Things has grown in recent years, data sharing has become one of the most beneficial cloud computing technologies. While the technology in question has a pleasing aesthetic, privacy continues to be one of its difficulties because inappropriate data utilization might have a number of unfavorable impacts. We offer a proxy re-encryption technique for cloud settings in this article in order to secure data transfer. Data owners can outsource their encrypted data to the cloud using identity-based encryption, and proxy re-encryption architecture makes sure that only authorized users can access the data. Because Internet of Things devices have limited capabilities, an edge device serves as a proxy server to do complex calculations. Moreover, we effectively allocate cached material in the proxy by utilizing information-centric networking capability, therefore attracting the degree of service through the effective utilization of the network capacity. Additionally, the foundation of our network model is the revolutionary technology known as block chain, which enables decentralized data sharing. It attains fine-grained control over access to data and diminishes bottlenecks in centrally managed systems. The safety research and assessment of our plan demonstrate the potential of our strategy for protecting data security, privacy, and integrity.

Title: Securing Serverless Environments: A Blockchain-Based Approach for Licensing and Payment Verification
Author: Sharma, Kriti; Kumar, Shivam; Saraswat, Om; Gupta, Nidhi
Abstract: Cracked software that exploits serverless computing resources has become a significant security concern for cloud providers, leading to cost inflation and heightened security risks. This paper examines how unauthorized software bypasses subscription models, triggering excessive resource consumption and Denial-of-Wallet (DoW) attacks. We explore the impact of these exploits on cloud service providers' financial stability and security. We propose detection mechanisms and preventive strategies to mitigate these risks, including anomaly detection and access control improvements, to protect both the platform and its users.
