Series: 2024 First International Conference on Pioneering Developments in Computer Science & Digital Technologies (IC2SDT)

Title: AI Technologies for Information Systems and Management Science, Proceedings of 6th International Conference on Information Systems and Management Science (ISMS) 2023 - Volume 2
Author: Agarwal, Saumye; Vardhan, Harsha Kothapalle; Prasanth, Narayanan; Devadas, T. Joshva; Naveenkumar, J.; Sureshkumar, Williams
Abstract: Cloud computing and cloud related services are gaining ground in today’s technology driven world. It allows an individual to delegate their work and store it in the cloud. The cloud provides pay per usage kind of services to the users. However, this model of services needs to ensure privacy and authentication so that only authorized users can access resources in the cloud. In this paper, we proposed a user authentication architecture that aims to improve user authentication for different cloud services and simultaneously incorporating a fine-grained access. A blockchain based approach is used to provide the security. We tested the architecture with two different scenarios and the result proves that the approach is effective and secure.
Series: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems

Title: Security Measures in Cloud-Driven Home Automation Systems
Author: Krishna, Dondapati Manoj; Pranay, Medasani Veda; Mohiddin, Shaik Khaja
Abstract: Cloud-driven home automation systems are widely used to enable high levels of convenience, efficiency, and connectivity as cloud technology becomes more and more integrated into everyday household operations. Despite these advantages, there is an increasing need to address security issues introduced by smart device interconnectivity and dependence on remote cloud services. Security features in cloud-based home automation systems are essential for guaranteeing the confidentiality, integrity, and dependability of data exchanges and smart device connectivity in residential environment. Strong security protocols and procedures are essential as homes become more networked and dependent on cloud services for automation and remote management. This study addresses the main issues, weak points, and recommended procedures for preventing cyberattacks and unwanted access as it focuses on the complex aspects of security in cloud-driven home automation systems. This study covers a wide range of security topics, including secure communication channels, data encryption, access controls, and authentication methods relevant to the home automation industry. By utilizing the knowledge from industry standards and cybersecurity research, this study looks at ways to mitigate common attack vectors, including malware infections, phishing scams, and unapproved device access. The study also explores the challenges of controlling user consent and privacy in cloud-driven home automation ecosystems, highlighting the significance of open data handling procedures and user-centric privacy controls. This study analyzes the methods employed to minimize data collection and storage, anonymize sensitive information, and provide users with fine-grained control over smart home environment.
Series: 2024 8th International Conference on Inventive Systems and Control (ICISC)

Title: A Secure Storage System for Financial Data based on Fuzzy Recognition Algorithms
Author: Yu, Xi; Timbang, Ferdinand Lapus
Abstract: This electronic document is a "live" template and already defines the coThe purpose of this paper is to develop a secure storage system for financial data based on fuzzy recognition algorithm to improve the security, accuracy and reliability of financial data and its applications. The system adopts the fuzzy C-means clustering algorithm to carry out intelligent analysis and processing of financial data. This paper begins to carry out specific research on the part of algorithm selection and algorithm implementation, and elaborates on the whole process, so as to explain the algorithm clearly and provide support for its subsequent application. The system test results show that the data encryption method and strict access control mechanism are used to ensure the security of data and the system has excellent performance in terms of data storage performance, encryption and decryption speed, API response time and system availability, throughput and error rate, etc., which can effectively meet the needs of safe, reliable and efficient financial data storage and management.

Title: Implementation of Secure Data Distribution System in Mobile Cloud Computing
Author: Maralkar, Prajakta; Mane, Kishor
Abstract: In today’s world the electronic technologies are developing at a very fast rate. The computational capability, storage capacity of computers or servers has also increased over the years. But as compared to this, the mobiles or smartphones have not developed. For running complex applications on mobile requires more computational capacity and storage space. To cope up with this can able to combine the power of mobile computing and cloud computing to improve the performance of mobile applications. While using Mobile Cloud Computing (MCC) there are number of other challenges like data privacy, data integrity, data security etc. In this paper, CBC algorithm is used to encrypt the data and provide security and access control. This system is simple to implement as compared to cloud-based systems. Each mobile user has to store short keys for authentication and decryption. The proposed system has different modules like data encryption and fragmentation, data upload, data retrieval and permission and data modification and data deletion. The system uses AES-CBC algorithm for encryption and bilinear signature (BLS) for checking integrity of data. For additional security, encrypted files are fragmented. The results show the communication and computation costs are reasonable which indicate efficient resource utilization, contributing to responsive data transmission and storage. The system demonstrates proper handling of diverse file operations, ensuring satisfactory performance across various file types and sizes. The system has robust security because of encryption and fragmentation.
Series: 2024 Asia Pacific Conference on Innovation in Technology (APCIT)

Title: Certificate Management for Cloud-Hosted Digital Twins
Author: Fotiou, Nikos; Kyriakidou, Chalima Dimitra Nassar; Papathanasiou, Athanasia Maria; Pittaras, Iakovos; Thomas, Yannis; Xylomenos, George
Abstract: A key enabler for the digitization of physical devices is digital twining technology. A digital twin is a virtual representation of a physical object (or a collection of physical objects) that allows their integration into cyber systems. Digital twins are usually hosted in cloud environments, which provide high availability and resilience to failures. This integration creates new opportunities and enables new capabilities, but it also raises security concerns. In this paper, we design a digital certificate management solution that allows building trust on digital twins independently of their network location. Our solution allows digital twins to securely receive certificates, which can be used to digitally sign data at the application layer. Our scheme does not depend on the certificate infrastructure used to secure the communication between end-users and the (cloud-hosted) digital twins. Our solution is feasible, realistic and resilient against key breaches, with a marginal communication overhead. Finally, our scheme automates the process of certificate issuance for digital twins, thus enabling very fast key and certificate rotation.
Series: 2024 IEEE Symposium on Computers and Communications (ISCC)

Title: Enhancing Healthcare Data Security in the Cloud: Integrating ML-Based Intrusion Detection Systems
Author: Sudha, K.; Nithyanandhan, R.; P, Anish T; Girija, P.; Nalini, M.; R, Siva Subramanian
Abstract: Technology integration, but particularly the merging of health care data systems (HCDS) with Cloud Computing, becomes crucial for the proper data management in developing healthcare system. The integration yields notable benefits including improved patient care, simplified administrative procedures and informed decision-making within healthcare organizations. Cloud computing also has scalability, flexibility and cost-effectiveness, so it becomes the best alternative for keeping and analyzing the big amounts of healthcare data. Nevertheless, the shift in paradigm leads to data security and privacy issues, which require strong security controls for sensitive health data. This research paper concerns optimizing HCDS using Cloud Computing to provide data management, accessibility, and scalability in the Healthcare industry. It studies the utilization of Technology, specifically Cloud Computing, in improving Health Care administration systems, reducing paperwork, and creating a centralized platform for efficient health care organization administration. The focus area is concerned with the security issues raised by keeping healthcare data on the cloud, which covers the creation and implementation of such as encryption, access controls and intrusion detection. The research utilizes the latest technologies such as AI and ML to enhance healthcare data on the cloud security. The NSL-KDD benchmark dataset is used to maturely apply and analyse ML models such as RF, SVM, and LR. The results show the models' capacity to distinguish Denial of Service, Probe, Remote and Local, and User to Root attacks. Compared to other ML models, in particular Random Forest is a leading one in performance in all attack types.
Series: 2024 2nd World Conference on Communication & Computing (WCONF)

Title: Assessing Secure Cloud Information Sharing Through Authentication and Encoded Indexing
Author: P, Pandiaraja; K, Karthik; P, Rajesh Kanna; C.Ushapriya; Mahesh, P.C.Senthil; K, Muthumanickam
Abstract: The high usage of storage in cloud, ensuring the privacy and security of information stored in the cloud has come up with a difficult concern. One approach to address this issue is the use of techniques which are encrypted, where data is already encrypted being uploaded to the storage of cloud. However, traditional encryption methods hinder the ability to find and retrieve particular information from the secured information, as the information needs to be decrypted first. This limitation hampers the usability and efficiency of storage of cloud systems. To overcome the challenge, this research says a novel approach for keyword search on secured information in storage of cloud using an AES approach. The algorithm of AES is a maximum adopted symmetric encryption method familiar for efficiency and robustness. By leveraging the AES encryption approach, the solution assures the confidentiality of information stored while enabling efficient keyword-based search operations without the need for decryption. The proposed approach utilizes a combination of cryptographic techniques such as AES encryption and index structures to access efficient information findings on the secured information. A secure index is created during encryption process that enables for potent retrieval of encrypted data related to specific keywords. The encrypted data remains confidential, as only authorized users possess the necessary decryption keys to retrieve the plaintext information. During data outsourcing, data owner can set the access permission based on their user identity. Users should have specific identity with decryption key for accessing data from cloud. Here data manager can also provide particular period for accessing information from cloud. The results demonstrate that the keyword findings on secured information in storage of using the AES approach achieve a balance between data privacy and search functionality. The solution offers an effective means to securely store and retrieve data from the cloud ensures that confidential data remains safeguarded against unauthorized access.

Title: Data Migration Approach under Secure Cloud Storage
Author: Thippamma, S.; Suhas, G.K.
Abstract: Many users currently store their files on many clouds, and it is not unusual for large amounts of data to be moved across clouds.It is possible that during the storage and transfer procedures, user files will get corrupted.This is because servers and cloud providers are not entirely reliable.Integrity verification must therefore be done, and it is best to spend as little time as possible on the process.The current techniques for demonstrating data migration still suffer with the issue of a large time overhead factor when it comes to large-scale file migrations.The authors of this article proposed a hierarchical proven data migration strategy to handle this problem.This method may be able to transfer a large number of continuous files between clouds while providing the efficacy of data transmission integrity authentication.This study offers a thorough explanation of the suggested approach along with an assessment of the security analysis's effectiveness.It was shown in light of the results that the proposed approach might significantly lower the detection latency of file transfers between clouds. © 2024 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Migration of Monolithic to Microservices With an Extraction Design Pattern in Single Sign on (SSO) Module Using Graph Neural Network (GNN)
Author: Mardhatillah, Laeila; Rochimah, Siti
Abstract: In software system development, Mololithic is an architectural model that is built in the same codebase. For example, on an online shopping site, there are several feature sections such as user authorization, shopping cart, payment, shipping, and others, all of these features are built in an integrated manner on the same codebase. This is different from the microservice architecture approach. In microservices, each feature or component will be an architecture that is separate from one another. Each of these services will later communicate with each other via a special protocol. Mololithic is increasingly being abandoned because it does not meet scalability needs, if there is a surge in users the Mololithic model tends to be unstable. As happens in the SSO module, in the SSO module process itself there are several functions including registration, authentication, user management, back end API and several other functions where these functions are combined in one unified module. Therefore, a Microservices Architecture model is needed to handle the needs due to the surge in users. Scalability can be regulated because the codebase separation process depends on needs. The migration process from monolithic to microservices is not easy, it requires sufficient knowledge regarding the application to determine the number of nodes and determine the number of services. This research will separate the codebase to determine the number of services using extraction design patterns on function entities, and system logs used in the SSO module at one institution in Indonesia. It is hoped that by extracting functions from the source code and data transaction we will get how many services are running and the nodes that will be used. The modeling process regarding the number of nodes and services will be carried out using a Graph Neural Network (GNN)

Author: Rajasekar, P; Kalaiselvi, K.; Shanmugam, Raju; Tamilselvan, S.; Pandian, A. Pasumpon
Abstract: Cloud computing caused the paradigm shift in business performance, from scalability to flexibility as well as affordability in the management of computing resources. Nevertheless, ensuring security of the data remains a key issue in the cloud due to the centralized interactions between service provider and a single vulnerability in the network can put rest of the data at risk. Consequently, the application of DLT, in addition to other solutions such as DLT, demonstrates a big step towards the improvement of cloud security frameworks. This article focuses on the implementation of DLT for data protection applications that are based on a solid dataset and decentralized security procedures in cloud environments. DLT utilization, like blockchain, provides an organization with integrity data, transparency, and fitness to counter cyber threats. Architecture stacks up sponsors such as cloud providers, users, and applications and DLT is responsible for the security of the transaction and the security policy enforcement. Customers use those services via desktop based application with transparent security policy arisen from DLT. Moreover, DLT also does identity management in the way that is decentralized, data sharing in the manner that it is secure, and the compliance to regulatory frameworks, which in addition reduces the trust and privacy risks in the cloud ecosystems. The proposed architecture is genuinely a big jump toward protecting cloud security from centralized control interruptions and thus, enhancing resilience and stability in cloud computing.

Title: Performance Evaluation of Off-Chain Storage Systems in Blockchain Environments
Author: R, Puneetha; R, Tanuja; H, Manjula S
Abstract: The Internet of Things(IoT) generates an exponential amount of data, and the data is heterogeneous and dynamic. The data has to be processed skillfully to unearth meaningful information from it. But, it is challenging for a human mind to process this data. Hence, data is stored either on a centralized server or on cloud platforms for future analytics. Whereas, centralized storage methods pose challenges with the underlying design being consolidated into a single authorization. Centralization leads to data misuse or manipulation and single-point failures. As a result, there was a paradigm shift towards emerging technologies such as Blockchain-based solutions. Blockchain technology has consistently attracted the attention of researchers and technological giants as an inevitable solution to the problems faced by centralized authorization and in enhancing the security and privacy of the data. However, storing massive amounts of data on Blockchain is not a viable solution since it is expensive and redundant. The widely accepted and researched resolution to this problem is offloading non-transactional data onto a decentralized storage widely on an InterPlanetary File System (IPFS). In this work, we analyze the security and privacy risks of storing sensitive data such as healthcare data, on IPFS by employing rigorous real-time data loads and retrievals on IPFS nodes in a private network setup, Docker environment. The performance is evaluated on the grounds of data availability and integrity. The results show the trend that IPFS is not a feasible solution for storing and transacting sensitive data to an extent.

Author: Rawal, Bharat S.
Abstract: This paper not only provides a comprehensive analysis of security and privacy risks based on upcoming 6G technologies at the physical, connection, and service levels, but it also provides insights acquired from the weaknesses of cutting-edge defenses and security designs. However, at this time, 6G privacy and security concerns are largely theoretical. The paper investigates privacy and security challenges in 5G and 6G wireless technologies and introduces a novel quantum safe access control handshake method for cloud and edge computing. We introduced a unique access control handshake process with NS sequence and RLP protocol, which provides enough complexity to consider as an NP-hard problem.

This paper introduces BCGeo, a novel architecture for decentralized geospatial services specifically tailored for smart healthcare systems. Addressing the limitations of traditional healthcare systems, BCGeo presents an online geospatial healthcare service designed for international residents of Bhubaneswar, India. The framework systematically tackles crucial technological issues, including data gathering, processing, access control, and privacy protection. BCGeo enhances healthcare service delivery through features like scalability, geospatial mapping, immutability, and patient prioritization. An analytical queueing system ensures efficient resource utilization, prioritizing urgent patient treatment. Decentralized privacy protection policies, enabled by Blockchain consensus, validate and anonymize data. Performance analysis, supported by detailed graphs and experimental data, verifies the efficiency of the proposed design. BCGeo marks a significant advancement in healthcare system design, offering an intelligent, accessible, and secure solution to contemporary healthcare challenges.

Title: Key Management and Authentication Scheme Forward Trusted Pervasive Container Computing
Author: Hei, XinHong; Xue, YuZhan; Wang, YiChuan; Liu, YiFan; Peng, Chen; Sun, Xiang
Abstract: Cloud computing technology is an internet-based computing model that provides high reliability and security measures, including data backup, secure access control, etc. As Docker containers play a increasingly important role in traditional cloud computing architectures, the communication needs between containers become prominent. However, existing container to container communication mainly relies on network protocols for file transfer, making it difficult to achieve the expected results in cloud cluster security. Therefore, this paper primarily focuses on container based keys and proposes a container identity trusted key management method based on Pervasive container computing architecture. The experimental results demonstrate that the container identity trusted key management method not only meets the security transmission characteristics required in the container cloud architecture, but also adopts a strategy combined with trusted hardware, providing security guarantees. In addition, the method proposed in this article that combines trusted hardware for signature verification can defend against multiple network attacks compared to traditional container architectures without using security policies.

Title: DeepShuffle: A Lightweight Defense Framework against Adversarial Fault Injection Attacks on Deep Neural Networks in Multi-Tenant Cloud-FPGA
Author: Luo, Yukui; Rakin, Adnan Siraj; Fan, Deliang; Xu, Xiaolin
Abstract: FPGA virtualization has garnered significant industry and academic interests as it aims to enable multi-tenant cloud systems that can accommodate multiple users’ circuits on a single FPGA. Although this approach greatly enhances the efficiency of hardware resource utilization, it also introduces new security concerns. As a representative study, one stateof-the-art (SOTA) adversarial fault injection attack, named Deep-Dup [1], exemplifies the vulnerabilities of off-chip data communication within the multi-tenant cloud-FPGA system. Deep-Dup attacks successfully demonstrate the complete failure of a wide range of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) in a black-box setup, by only injecting fault to extremely small amounts of sensitive weight data transmissions, which are identified through a powerful differential evolution searching algorithm. Such emerging adversarial fault injection attack reveals the urgency of effective defense methodology to protect DNN applications on the multi-tenant cloud-FPGA system. This paper, for the first time, presents a novel movingtarget-defense (MTD) oriented defense framework DeepShuffle, which could effectively protect DNNs on multi-tenant cloudFPGA against the SOTA Deep-Dup attack, through a novel lightweight model parameter shuffling methodology. DeepShuffle effectively counters the Deep-Dup attack by altering the weight transmission sequence, which effectively prevents adversaries from identifying security-critical model parameters from the repeatability of weight transmission during each inference round. Importantly, DeepShuffle represents a training-free DNN defense methodology, which makes constructive use of the typologies of DNN architectures to achieve being lightweight. Moreover, the deployment of DeepShuffle neither requires any hardware modification nor suffers from any performance degradation. We evaluate DeepShuffle on the SOTA open-source FPGA-DNN accelerator, Vertical Tensor Accelerator (VTA), which represents the practice of real-world FPGA-DNN system developers. We then evaluate the performance overhead of DeepShuffle and find it only consumes an additional ∼3% of the inference time compared to the unprotected baseline. DeepShuffle improves the robustness of various SOTA DNN architectures like VGG, ResNet, etc. against Deep-Dup by orders. It effectively reduces the efficacy of evolution searching-based adversarial fault injection attack close to random fault injection attack, e.g., on VGG-11, even after increasing the attacker’s effort by 2.3×, our defense shows a ∼93% improvement in accuracy, compared to the unprotected baseline.

Title: SCWAD: Automated Pentesting of Web Applications
Author: Talon, Natan; Tong, Valérie; Guette, Gilles; Han, Yufei; Laarouchi, Youssef
Abstract: A wide array of techniques and tools can be employed for web application security assessment. Some methods, such as fuzzers and scanners, are partially or fully automated, offering speed and cost-effectiveness. However, these tools often fall short in detecting specific vulnerabilities like broken access control and are prone to generating false positives. On the other hand, manual processes like penetration testing, though more time-consuming and necessitating expertise, provide a more comprehensive risk assessment. To overcome the limitations of automated tools, these techniques are frequently combined. Fuzzers and scanners, despite their ease of use and quick results, require the expertise of penetration testing experts to address their limitations. By integrating these approaches, a more robust and nuanced security assessment can be achieved. This article presents SCWAD, an automated and customizable penetration testing framework designed to assess vulnerabilities in web applications. © 2024 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: IDENTITY-BASED PRIVACY-PRESERVING ANONYMOUS AUTHENTICATION ACCESS CONTROL FOR SECURE CLOUD COMPUTING
Author: Praneetha, N; Rao, S Srinivasa; R, Maheswara Rao V V; Rao, I S Siva; Brahmanandam, P S
Journal: Proceedings on Engineering Sciences
Abstract: The storage of data with access controllability in sharing data between multiple users in a dispersed environment is now the most pressing issue in cloud computing. Cloud computing's unique feature allows its subscribers to exchange and manage their data with one another safely. However, privacy is essential for all cloud users to communicate freely and openly, as data is accessed by unwanted parties in the cloud. Cloud services have employed numerous security-related techniques for efficient and safe user data exchange. These methods provide efficient, flexible, and reliable access control rules between users when exchanging data. But, they each have advantages and disadvantages concerning key generation and data security. To address the need for adaptable, scalable, and trustworthy access control while exchanging data across a dispersed network, this research proposes a novel access control-based privacy-preserving approach. In terms of cipher text and critical policy security, this method is an extension of attribute-based encryption and the only difference is that with cloud computing, users hierarchically share data, and access control policy amongst shared users is evaluated efficiently. Our method includes sophisticated security features like the revocation of users and access rights of users for outsourced data in the cloud. It also provides scalability and dependability in producing critical structures with dynamic qualities. Experimental results demonstrate that the suggested method improves the current system in terms of cloud data sharing efficiency, scalability, and dependability. © 2024 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Modelling a Request and Response-Based Cryptographic Model For Executing Data Deduplication in the Cloud
Author: India, Computer Science and Engineering, Koneru Lakshmaiah Education Foundation, Guntur, Andhra Pradesh,; Nulaka, Nulaka; Srinivasu, Nulaka
Journal: Journal of Cybersecurity and Information Management
Abstract: Cloud storage is one of the most crucial components of cloud computing because it makes it simpler for users to share and manage their data on the cloud with authorized users. Secure deduplication has attracted much attention in cloud storage because it may remove redundancy from encrypted data to save storage space and communication overhead. Many current safe deduplication systems usually focus on accomplishing the following characteristics regarding security and privacy: Access control, tag consistency, data privacy and defence against various attacks. But as far as we know, none can simultaneously fulfil all four conditions. In this research, we offer a safe deduplication method that is effective and provides user-defined access control to address this flaw. Because it only allows the cloud service provider to grant data access on behalf of data owners, our proposed solution (Request-response-based Elliptic Curve Cryptography) may effectively delete duplicates without compromising the security and privacy of cloud users. A thorough security investigation reveals that our approved safe deduplication solution successfully thwarts brute-force attacks while dependably maintaining tag consistency and data confidentiality. Comprehensive simulations show that our solution surpasses the evaluation in computing, communication, storage overheads, and deduplication efficiency.

Title: Enhancing Effectiveness and Security in Microservices Architecture
Author: Matias, Michael; Ferreira, Ernesto; Mateus-Coelho, Nuno; Ferreira, Luís
Abstract: Microservices have allowed the decomposition of large monoliths and introduced the simple responsibility principle into its essence. It allowed complex systems to be more cost efficient and easily scalable. With this new architecture, new vulnerabilities were introduced, such as the large surface that started to get exposed to the internet. Instead of having one monolithic surface exposed, we started to have several small services exposed. New patterns were introduced to try to diminish these threats and among them the “API Gateway” pattern was introduced. The purpose of this article is to further explore the API Gateway pattern, and to further enhance the microservices communication security as part of that pattern. This research proposes a hybrid approach, using HTTPS and JWT only when strictly necessary, towards overcoming those recognized limitations of security and performance. Furthermore, proof of concept on top of NB-IoT communication protocol was developed. It intends to explore the transmission of a large quantity of low-frequency data from devices to the cloud, while the communication maintains effective and with low latency. The created supporting microservices API followed the proposed architecture and was tested against security attacks towards mitigating its impacts.

Author: Ananthakrishna, V.; Yadav, C.S.

Abstract: Security is of utmost importance in the dynamic field of cloud computing. This study offers a comprehensive analysis of the latest advancements in cloud security, focusing specifically on a developing paradigm. The suggested technique combines Enhanced AuthPrivacyChain with hybrid encryption to provide a distinctive encryption solution. The aim of this study is to conduct a thorough analysis and evaluation of the present state of secure cloud computing. It addresses the significant issue of scalability by doing an analysis of more than 50 pertinent research publications. The proposed method improves the AuthPrivacyChain framework, a blockchain-based access control system, by providing an innovative hybrid encryption architecture. This solution deliberately combines the attributes of symmetric and asymmetric encryption, using their unique qualities to enhance the security of cloud data. The primary objectives are to attain precise access control, deter unauthorized access, and enable effective administration of encrypted data in cloud environments. The assessment emphasizes the significance of attribute-based encryption, homomorphic encryption, and multi-party computing in bolstering the security of data stored in the cloud. This conclusion is derived from the assessment of the chosen references. The AuthPrivacyChain architecture enhances security by using blockchain technology, which guarantees strong privacy safeguards and accountability in cloud transactions. Furthermore, the hybrid encryption model adeptly overcomes the constraints linked to conventional encryption methods, providing a meticulous equilibrium between security and performance. The literature that has been consistently researched underscores the need of improving scalability. The proposed technique may successfully handle the increasing demands of cloud computing environments by efficiently handling the growing number and complexity of data while maintaining strict security regulations. This review article is an essential resource for academics, business workers, and policymakers who are deeply engaged in the field of cloud security. By integrating knowledge from various sources, our work not only adds to the current discussion on protecting cloud data, but also establishes a foundation for future progress in the field, promoting creativity and resilience in the face of changing cybersecurity threats. and resilience in the face of evolving cybersecurity challenges. © 2024 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Author: Keshattiwar, Prasad; Lokulwar, Prasad; Saraf, Pranay
Abstract: Ensuring sensitive data security is critical in the ever changing world of cloud computing. This paper offers an overview of our all-encompassing security protocols, created to tackle the ever-changing demands of contemporary information ecosystems. Proposed approach starts with a strong encryption architecture that uses the most recent algorithms to protect data while it’s in transit and at rest. We proactively identify and neutralise such attacks before they have a chance to jeopardise the integrity of the cloud environment by utilizing sophisticated AI-driven anomaly detection. A proactive approach to addressing new security threats is ensured by this real-time threat mitigation. A multi-layered authentication and access control system that customises rights depending on user roles and responsibilities is another feature of Empowering Data Defender. By using this granular approach, sensitive material is protected from unauthorised access and only authorised workers can interact with it. Project approach includes regular security audits and compliance inspections to make sure that industry standard and laws are followed. In addition to strengthening the present security posture, this ongoing monitoring and assessment procedure allows for quick adaptability to changing compliance needs. Encouraging Data Defender’s all-encompassing security approach fortifies cloud-based data, fostering confidence and trust in the digital age. Through the integration of access control, intrusion prevention, encryption, and compliance measures, our methodology provides a holistic resolution to the complex problems presented by contemporary cloud systems

Because of its adaptability, businesses can keep up with changing cyberthreats by continuously improving and modifying their defences against new attacks. By means of the well-balanced combination of sophisticated encryption and access control, this technical marvel acts as a formidable guardian, enabling businesses to take use of the cloud’s boundless potential while safeguarding their most precious resource.

Title: Improving the Security and Reliability of SDN Controller REST APIs Using JSON Web Token (JWT) with OpenID and auth2.0
Author: ELHejazi, Mahmoud F.; Muragaa, Wisam H. A
Abstract: As Software-Defined Networking (SDN) continues to gain popularity, the need for secure and efficient methods of authenticating users and controlling access to network resources becomes increasingly important. RESTful APIs are commonly used in SDN to enable communication between applications and network devices through the controllers. However, without proper authentication mechanisms, these APIs can be vulnerable to attacks such as injection and unauthorized access. This paper proposes lighter and reliable REST API authentication solution with less open configuration for Software-Defined Networking (SDN) controllers based on JSON Web Token (JWT), OpenID and auth2.0. The proposed solution offers a secure and efficient way to authenticate and authorize users, control access to network resources, and protect against injection attacks. It consists of generating a secret key, defining the JWT payload, generating the JWT, including the JWT in the HTTP Authorization header, verifying the JWT, extracting the payload from the JWT, and implementing token refresh. The solution is implemented using a combination of libraries in Python [requests-json-http.client] and tested on an SDN controller using a cisco DNA sandbox network environment. The results show that the proposed authentication solution is highly efficient and effective, making it suitable for use in high-performance SDN environments. It provides a much-needed solution for securing RESTful APIs in SDN controllers, and we hope that it will encourage further research in this area.

This abstract presents examining new techniques for the detection of security among cloud web applications with the capabilities of IoT. Through the equipment of IoT devices, there will be the enhancement of real-time monitoring and detection of safety threats in cloud-based applications that are Internet-based. This synergy enables banks to have access to a variety of data sources, that is, both internal and external data. It makes the collection of large volumes of data possible, and so the banks have a good picture of the environment in which the application runs. With the use of machine learning and AI algorithms in the background, the existing anomalies and known potential vulnerabilities can be found fast, hence paving the way for proactive remediation of the present and future threats. Author: Lima, Vinícius Costa; Crepaldi, Nathalia Yukie; Bernardi, Filipe Andrade; Segamarchi, Renan Barbieri; Alves, Domingos
Abstract: This study describes the System for Tuberculosis Control - SISTB, a health information system designed to manage TB cases. Tuberculosis remains a major worldwide health challenge, necessitating excellent data management and collaboration to provide effective patient care and disease control. SISTB satisfies these imperatives by delivering a platform with many helpful features, including treatment follow-up and daily supervision of medication intake. The essential elements of the system are a web-based application and web services to enable communication with external systems. In addition, the SISTB system has a Semantic API that extracts contextualized data from web pages using semantic annotations. Sensitive health information is protected by a robust security layer that includes authentication, authorization, data integrity checks, and hybrid cryptography. This work emphasizes SISTB’s ability to integrate external data via its middleware engine and highlights the potential to improve data-driven activities, expedite patient care, and contribute to more successful tuberculosis control activities, focusing on enhancing TB case management.

Title: Design and Implementation of a Blockchain-Based User Access Control Model
Author: Wang, Ziheng; Li, Zhaolong; Li, Xiaozhen; Li, Jicheng; Zhang, Qian; Cao, Hongyu; Meng, Yu
Abstract: User access control systems are essential components across various applications and websites, providing operational managers the ability to control user access to information. However, as the number of users grows, using a single management center no longer meets the demands of massive user access requests. Blockchain technology, characterized by decentralization and immutability, shows immense potential in user access management. Ad-dressing the limited processing speed and inadequate security of single management centers, this paper introduces a blockchain-based user access control model. It designs a blockchain structure with designated servers as nodes, explores attribute-based access control mechanisms, and develops processing mechanisms for different requests. The paper also simulates massive user requests, tests the performance of the proposed architecture under scenarios of massive requests, and compares it with other access control models. The results demonstrate that the proposed user access control model achieves superior performance in scenarios with massive requests compared to other models.

Title: Fog Computing for Intelligent Cloud IoT Systems
Author: Das, Malabika
Abstract: Attribute‐based encryption is a generalization of public key cryptography based on one‐to‐many encryptions that allow users to encrypt and decrypt data based on user attributes. It is different from identity‐based encryption, in which access control is based on the identities of users such as their email addresses, and usernames. In ABE, each user is associated with a set of attributes. These attributes can be various characteristics such as jobs, organizations, age groups, or any other criteria. In decentralized attribute‐based encryption, any party can create a public key and private key for different users which reflect their attributes without any collaboration. ABE has been widely used to impose fine‐grained access control on encrypted data. Fine‐grained access control is a method of controlling who can access certain data. It is essential because it sets access parameters for specific data even when data is stored together, which means it specifies the access rights of individual users. It is often used in cloud computing where a large amount of data is stored together and it gives each piece of data its own specified policy for access. For example, one individual may be given access to edit and make changes to a piece of data while another might be given access only to read the data without making any changes. Fog computing extends the cloud computing paradigm to the edge of the network. The main difference between fog computing and cloud computing is decentralization and flexibility. Fog computing brings computing to the networks’ edge by moving storage and computing systems as near as possible to the applications, components, and devices that need thus reducing processing latency and improving efficiencies. Fog computing implementation involves either writing or porting IoT devices at the network edge for fog nodes using fog tools. Those nodes take in the data from the other edge devices and then direct the data into the optimal location for analysis.

Title: Intelligent Systems Design and Applications, Information and Network Security, Volume 3
Author: Gupta, Shubham; Kukreja, Swetta; Parasar, Deepa; Kazi, Naufil
Abstract: This study investigates effective ways to prevent web application exploitation and account takeovers. It emphasizes the need to secure online accounts against evolving digital threats by analyzing various vulnerabilities like XSS, CSRF, broken authentication, password attacks, and business logic flaws. The paper uniquely examines advanced attack techniques such as Unicode mapping collision, OAuth threats, host header injection, and response manipulation, detailing their reproduction steps. It proposes mitigation strategies including secure coding, input validation, robust session management, two-factor authentication, and user awareness, advancing over current practices. By offering a detailed analysis of attack methods and countermeasures, the study contributes significantly to web security research, providing practical solutions and setting a benchmark for future work in this area.

Title: Dynamic Password Verification Method for USER IDENTITY IN CLOUD R&D Environment
Author: Zhang, Chi; Zhang, Xiaodong; Xu, Qiaoling; Ma, Dongdong; Yang, Jianwei
Abstract: With the rapid development of cloud computing, more and more organizations migrate their business to the cloud and begin to use the R&D environment on the cloud. In order to improve the security and efficiency of user authentication and access control in cloud environment, a dynamic password verification method of user identity in cloud R&D environment is studied. Generating a security combination key in the cloud environment, a key matrix was given, and the user identity and the corresponding password were verified. The basic authentication model of user identity was constructed, the authentication categories were classified from the perspective of security and application, and the secure communication between the server and the client was ensured. Innovative verification of dynamic password based on encryption function, receiving and interpreting key content, user identity dynamic password was verified, and the verification speed and convenience were improved. The experimental results show that the initial compression rate of this method is 96%, and when the user authentication information in PC is 20KB, the compression result is 214B. The dynamic password verification time is kept at 0.2 seconds, which ensures the application effect. This proves that this method can provide secure, efficient and flexible authentication services for various cloud service platforms. The experimental results show that when the user authentication information in PC is 20KB, the compression result is 214B. The dynamic password verification time is kept at 0.2s. This proves that this method can provide safe, efficient and flexible authentication services for various cloud service platforms.

Title: Algorithms in Advanced Artificial Intelligence
Author: Tamilkodi, R.; Kala, K. Surya; Sukanthika, T. Durga; Kiran, B. Aanantha Sai Datta; Reddy, V. Hemanth; Neha, K.Srimani
Abstract: The issue at hand is that as cloud computing grows, there is growing worry about cloud security. Sensitive data stored in the cloud is susceptible to illegal access or alteration by hackers or internal cloud administrators when centralized access control methods are in place. The security and integrity of corporate and personal data are seriously threatened by this. One proposed answer for this issue is AuthPrivacyChain, a blockchain based access control architecture AuthPrivacyChain uses blockchain node addresses as identities to renegotiate permissions for cloud data access control. These permissions are kept on the blockchain and are encrypted. Processes for authorization, revocation, and access control are also included in the framework. When AuthPrivacyChain is used on an enterprise operating system such as EOS, it significantly improves cloud security by guarding against unwanted access and guaranteeing the privacy of authorized users.

Title: Intelligence Computation and Applications, 14th International Symposium, ISICA 2023, Guangzhou, China, November 18–19, 2023, Revised Selected Papers, Part II
Author: Jiang, Chengyu; Ma, Sha; Wang, Hao
Abstract: Cloud computing changes our way of life by offering advantages in convenience and cost savings. However, the security and privacy issues associated with this technology should not be taken lightly. In various cloud computing applications such as shared contacts, categorization of users on social applications, and unpublished papers plagiarism detection, public key encryption with equality test (PKEET) plays a significant role in their privacy protection. In the existing PKEET schemes, the authorization algorithms can only authorize an encrypted data or all encrypted data, but cannot authorize any encrypted data collections. In addition, the majority of these schemes use computationally expensive pairing operations. Based on this, we propose a new pairing free scheme that can authorize specified sets of encrypted data thereby reducing the number of authorization trapdoors. Additionally, our scheme demonstrates high efficiency in simulation experiment compared to related works.

Title: Integrating Blockchain in Cloud Computing for Enhanced Data Management and Security
Author: Choubey, Abha; Choubey, Siddhartha; Jaiswal, Dipti; Jaiswal, Manuraj
Abstract: This article details a decentralized cloud data management and protection scheme. The Decentralized Data Storage Algorithm, Smart Contracts for Access Control Algorithm, Consensus Mechanisms for Data Validation Algorithm, Blockchain-based Encryption Algorithm, and Tokenization of Data Algorithm solve important data storage, access control, validation, encryption, and tokenization problems. Each piece of software is carefully designed to add features to the system. The Decentralized Data Storage Algorithm secures data via blockchain and agreement processes. The Smart Contracts for Access Control Algorithm dynamically limits access based on user passwords and policy outcomes. Autonomous systems need the Consensus Mechanisms for Data Validation Algorithm to maintain trust and freedom. The blockchain-based encryption algorithm secures data via blockchain keys and encryption. Finally, the tokenization of data algorithms emphasizes data security and transport. Ablation research emphasizes each mathematical component and how they work together to improve the framework. Performance tables and graphs show that the recommended method improves cloud computing data management and security. This method addresses the developing issues of cloud data management in a thorough and adaptable manner, making it valuable to the area.

Title: Implementation of Multi Extension in Blockchain-Based IoT Platform for Industrial IoT Devices
Author: Prayudi, Agus; Sukaridhoto, Sritrusta; Rasyid, Muhammad Udin Harun Al; Hakim, Oktafian Sultan; Panduman, Yohanes Yohanie Fridelin; Budiarti, Rizqi Putri Nourma
Journal: JOIV : International Journal on Informatics Visualization
Abstract: The rise of the Internet of Things (IoT) has led to the creation of technologies to improve human life. IoT involves integrating the Internet with the physical world, spanning applications like smart homes, industries, supply chains, academia, and more. By the end of 2020, around 212 billion IoT devices were globally deployed, presenting substantial opportunities for manufacturers and diverse applications. There have been numerous implementations of IoT across various fields, including Blockchain IoT (B-IoT), Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT), Digital Twin, and new communication protocols like the Matter protocol. We conducted a comprehensive testing of the blockchain (B-IoT) extension system on various bandwidths and scenarios, such as blockchain API execution time, speed, retention performance, and smart contract vulnerability testing. Our testing has been successful, and several messaging systems were used. Kafka was recommended to overcome the pending transaction problem caused by unprocessed messages. Our smart contract exhibited high severity. The Artificial Intelligence of Things extension, tested on real environments for person and vehicle counters, has shown successful results. Digital Twin, integrated into the IoT platform to perform and control 3D assets such as the postgraduate PENS building, has demonstrated efficient performance. Matter protocol achieved an average task execution speed of 0.48 tasks per second. Matter P2P communication was also successfully tested in this research by implementing the Access Control List (ACL) command.

Title: Design and Implementation of an Electricity Market Trading Platform Architecture for High Concurrency Access by Market Entities
Author: Shao, Ping; Liu, Yonghui; Huang, Longda; Tian, Ying; Xu, Pan
Abstract: The electricity market trading platform faces the challenge of high-concurrency access due to the massive entry of market entities. A new architecture for the electricity market trading platform is required to meet the high-concurrency access needs of millions of market entities while ensuring the security, stability, and efficiency of transactions. This design employs load balancing, microservices technology, containerization, priority-based concurrent access control, and hybrid cloud segmentation to construct an expandable, reliable, and maintainable electricity market trading platform. Testing has validated the reliability and performance advantages of the designed platform architecture, providing technical insights and references for the future research and innovation of electricity trading platforms.

Title: Decentralized File Storage Platform using IPFS and Blockchain
Author: Nalina, V; Navaneeth, S; Nayak, Rahul Anil; Prakash, Nidhi
Abstract: This paper presents a pioneering web application that combines Inter Planetary File System (IPFS) and Blockchain technology to meet the increasing demand for secure, scalable, and decentralized data storage. The system utilizes locally-hosted Digital Ocean droplets as gateways, eliminating reliance on third-party companies and maintaining decentralization. By integrating blockchain technology, the application enhances security through transaction authentication and access permission management. It offers features such as access control, file integrity checking using IPFS hashes, and the potential for future enhancements like a custom cryptocurrency for transactions. This innovative system provides a practical, decentralized alternative to mainstream cloud storage services, ensuring data privacy, security, and integrity while granting users greater authority over their data.

Title: Design and Implementation of High Concurrency Access Dynamic Control Strategy Considering the Priority of Electricity Market Business
Author: Shao, Ping; Liu, Yonghui; Wang, Haichao; Xu, Pan; Pan, Jiajia
Abstract: This paper presents a dynamic control strategy for high concurrency access with priority in electricity market businesses. The strategy integrates advanced information technology methods with a deep understanding of electricity market business characteristics to ensure the system can rapidly respond and accurately process various businesses, especially those with higher priority in electricity market transactions, in a high concurrency environment. The proposed strategy includes a business priority recognition and mapping mechanism, a priority-based dynamic scheduling algorithm, and a multi-level concurrency control strategy. The implementation of the strategy utilizes a microservices architecture, with services independently deployed, scaled, and maintained. The strategy was deployed and tested in a simulation test environment, with the results demonstrating its effectiveness in handling high concurrency access and improving system throughput, response time, and resource utilization.

Title: Secure Communication in Internet of Things, Emerging Technologies, Challenges, and Mitigation
Author: Reshmi, T. R.; Abhishek, Kunal
Abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) security encompasses the protection of various components including devices, cloud infrastructure, software, mobile applications, network interfaces, encryption methods, authentication protocols, and physical security measures. The vulnerabilities in IoT application data security, outlined by the Open Web Application Security Project (OWASP), stem from issues like insecure web interfaces, inadequate authentication/authorization, flawed software/firmware, privacy apprehensions, insecure network services, absence of transport encryption, compromised cloud interfaces, vulnerable mobile interfaces, limited security configurability, weak physical security, and both application and endpoint security. Cellular IoT confronts a range of signaling attacks, including threats to identification, location privacy breaches, data interception, tapping, and denial of service. In the context of 5G-IoT, the sudden surge in interconnected mesh networks facilitated by IoT devices introduces critical security challenges. The conventional hub-and-spoke model has been fundamentally transformed with the incorporation of edge computing techniques. In this meshed environment, any weak point can potentially become a security vulnerability, heightening the importance of robust security measures in the 5G- and 6G-enabled IoT landscape. The chapter primarily centers around in-depth discussions concerning these security issues and provides insights into potential avenues for future research aimed at mitigating these challenges.

Title: Secure Communication in Internet of Things, Emerging Technologies, Challenges, and Mitigation
Author: Dahiwale, Prashant; Raghuwanshi, M. M.; Mate, Sanjay
Abstract: The way we interact with the world around us has been totally revolutionized by the Internet of Things (IoT) by allowing for greater automation and connectivity. However, the continuously increased number of IoT devices increases the potential for security vulnerability. With the use of cloud technology, IoT offers a number of benefits including scalability, flexibility, and cost-effectiveness but it also presents unique security challenges. This chapter explores the current state of cloud security in IoT including common threats and attack vectors, and examines the various security measures that can be implemented to mitigate these risks. Key topics discussed include encryption, access control, authentication, and secure communication protocol. Additionally, the chapter highlights the importance of continuous monitoring and threat detection in maintaining the security of cloud-based IoT systems. By understanding the security risks and implementing appropriate safeguards, organizations can maximize the benefits of cloud technology in IoT while minimizing the potential for security breaches.

Title: Cloud-based electronic health record sharing and access controlling blockchain architecture using data de-identification method
Author: Muid, Munshi Rejwan Ala; Jubaida, Afrin; Onik, Md. Mehedi Hasan; Hamid, Hamim
Journal: International Journal of Medical Engineering and Informatics
Abstract: Electronic health record (EHR) demands the highest privacy and security as the accuracy of medical research and service largely depend on the integrity of it. Intruders can tamper sensitive protected health information (PHI) or personally identifiable information (PII) purposefully. This study aims to use blockchain technology to build a complete EHR sharing and tracking system, such that even after access is granted to researchers or medical personnel, EHRs remain unaltered and the identities of patients are hidden. This work uses a traditional cloud storage system to store information while saving the indexes of EHRs in a chain to ensure PHI integrity. Additionally, data sharing is secured by applying a randomly selected data de-identification method that guarantees integrity and trackability of user data anonymously. Finally, this work demonstrates a complete architectural implementation (using Hyperledger and a private blockchain network) of the proposed EHR sharing and access controlling by using two levels of chain (two distinct ledgers) that ensures an efficient sharing platform of PHI.

Title: Smart Technologies in Healthcare Management, Pioneering Trends and Applications
Author: Jain, Aryan; Sindhwani, Nidhi; Vashisth, Rashmi; Chauhan, Sudhir
Abstract: In recent years, the use of cloud computing has grown in popularity, as organizations look to take advantage of the scalability, flexibility, and cost-effectiveness of this technology. This chapter aims to explore the issue of data privacy in cloud integration, including the various security measures that can be used to safeguard cloud-stored data, as well as the legal and regulatory problems regarding data privacy. In addition, the role of third-party corporations and organizations in preserving data stored in the cloud will be examined, as will the ethical and moral implications of data privacy in cloud integration. Data privacy in cloud integration necessitates the adoption of strong security measures to prevent unauthorized access to sensitive data and ensure compliance with data protection laws. Organizations must carefully assess cloud service providers’ security features and ensure that adequate security steps are in place to safeguard their data. Furthermore, to reduce the risk of data breaches and guarantee data protection in cloud integration, organizations must implement best practises such as data encryption, access controls, and frequent security assessments. Effective communication and cooperation between cloud service providers and their customers is also required to handle any security concerns and ensure confidential data is protected. Furthermore, the talk will discuss the present state of the art and best practises in data science, privacy in cloud incorporation, providing insights and recommendations to businesses contemplating cloud computing.

Title: Intelligent Poka Yoke System for Secure and Efficient Industrial Equipment Monitoring and Control
Author: Arun, C.A; Manohar, Relangi Sanjay; Krishan, G Kirupa; Khan, Menaz; Sharma, Aditya; Raj, Tanya
Abstract: Ensuring the safety and efficiency of manufacturing processes is required in Industry 4.0. To address this, an intelligent Poka Yoke system is proposed, specifically designed for monitoring and controlling Industry Programmable Logic Controller machines. This system prioritizes security by requiring strict staff authorization, providing timely alerts, and granting access privileges based on predetermined criteria. It efficiently prevents unauthorized access and minimizes potential industrial dangers by leveraging modern technology such as employee access keys and NFC authentication. NFC is used to authenticate employee credentials, allowing access to only approved jobs by using Raspberry Pi Pico as a controller. The technology detects anomalies and safety threats in real time while continuously monitoring equipment operations. The generated data is virtualized in a user-friendly web application, conveniently stored in Mongo dB cloud, allowing for instant notifications and automated equipment shutdown when necessary. This system improves workplace security, safety, and efficiency by streamlining operations and increasing productivity.

Title: A Review of IoT Security: Machine Learning and Deep Learning Perspective
Author: Dubey, Krati; Dubey, Rishav; Panedy, Sudhakar; Kumar, Sanjay
Abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) gives the ability to people and machines to interact and learn from billions of items, including sensors, actuators, services, and other things that are connected to the Internet. The services provided by IoT are becoming an indispensable part of human life, further, the growth in the number of IoT devices is predicted to increase exponentially in the next few years. However, the IoT network consists of a variety of different types of devices being placed in heterogeneous environments. The data these devices generate contains noise in significant proportion. Also, these devices are vulnerable to various different kinds of attacks, identification of which is a challenging task in itself as they are in large numbers. The detection of faults is necessary for the early stages. Generic methods of authentication and authorization are not sufficient for these devices. Further, we need methods that can detect the attack at an early stage based on previous patterns and alert the system at the right time. In recent years machine learning and deep learning (ML/DL) algorithms have advanced considerably from being an experimental project in the research community to being applied in industry-standard applications. These algorithms have the potential to be better than simple security methods in providing intelligence to the system. In this article, we have reviewed various ML/DL algorithms with their advantages, and disadvantages, and how they can be applied in securing IoTs. Initially, a detailed overview of IoT, components, and applications are presented. After that, we present an overview of various threats, and attack methods are discussed with the probable ML/DL solutions.

Title: Advances in Emerging Information and Communication Technology
Author: Almushiti, Elaf; Zaki, Raseel; Thamer, Nora; Alshaya, Rima
Abstract: In the OWASP Top 10 Version 2021, the Broken Access Control is ranked first position. That means it is the most exploited vulnerability today by attackers. Because if the attacker can break the access control, he can take administrator privileges and compromise the entire web application. After that, he can launch any type of attack for his purpose. That was the cause of why it was most targeted. In this search, we will present the Broken Access Control vulnerability. First, we talk about its history and then present an overview. After that, we show some research related to our search. Then we reviewed the web application vulnerabilities that attackers may exploit to break the access control. Finally, we talk about protection and security that should be taken against attackers who exploit this vulnerability.

Title: Design and Implementation of a Web-Based Platform for Administering a Virtual University
Author: Sabah, Imad Fadhil
Abstract: the expansion and dominance of the internet requires reliable and secure management platforms for a variety of academic and administrative tasks. This paper is aimed at presenting the design of a web-based platform that is designed for the management of a virtual institution. Using the literature review method, the research identifies major challenges and requirements for virtual university administration, in particular the necessity to address security concerns, ensure user friendliness of interfaces, and increase design flexibility. The system design involves the use of secure file storage systems, access control mechanisms, and the utilization of web application firewall among other security measures against cyber-attacks. The adoption of responsive design frameworks ensures that services are compatible with a wide range of devices and increases the level of accessibility and experience of users. Critiques show that the platform meets the functional needs, privacy, and security needs, as well as the general usability of the system. The article ends by proposing future research suggestions that include the development of more secure systems, personalization of learning processes, and the inclusion of mobile applications to enhance the administration of the virtual university.

Title: Revolutionizing Healthcare: Cloud-Based Health Information Exchange and Disease Prediction
Author: Nithin, S.N.; Vishwas, V.; Gudapareddy, M.P.R.; Peddineni, V.; Beena, B.M.
Abstract: A cloud-based system called Health Information Exchange (HIE) is. Hosted on Amazon Web Services (AWS). This system provides logins, for doctors, administrators and patients. The primary objective of this work is to revolutionize healthcare data sharing by providing a convenient platform. Patients are empowered to manage their health by selecting their symptoms and receiving disease predictions. AWS is utilized to orchestrate the cloud-based infrastructure, which includes SageMaker for constructing machine learning models RDS for a PostgreSQL database, EC2 for hosting the Django server, Lambda for deploying machine learning model APIs CloudWatch for resource monitoring and IAM, for access control. The core element of this system is the implementation of a classification framework that optimizes the organization and retrieval of data. This innovative approach enhances data accessibility while streamlining healthcare processes to facilitate decision making and patient care. By integrating AWS services, it also creates a scalable foundation that supports the growth of a dynamic retail environment. © 2024 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Secure Data Transfer onto Cloud Environment using Diffie-Hellman Key Exchange Algorithm
Author: Bhansali, Aayushi; Harisha, Juluru; Sinha, Garima
Abstract: This research study addresses the importance of maintaining personal privacy in various cloud computing usage scenarios, considering the specific benefits and risks associated with each environment. It presents a robust solution for secure data transfer using cloud technology, focusing on protecting sensitive information during transit. The solution integrates advanced encryption protocols and secure communication channels to ensure end-to-end protection. Additionally, access controls and authentication mechanisms are employed to authorize legitimate recipients. The cloud infrastructure offers scalability and efficiency for seamless data exchange across diverse environments. Rigorous testing validates the system's resilience against potential vulnerabilities, providing a reliable and confidential data transfer process. Overall, this research study meets the critical need for safeguarding information integrity in today's dynamic digital landscape, offering a practical and effective solution.

Title: Uncovering the Risk of Academic Information System Vulnerability through PTES and OWASP Method
Author: Utama, Ferzha Putra; Nurhadi, Raden Muhammad Hilmi
Journal: CommIT (Communication and Information Technology) Journal
Abstract: The security of academic information systems needs consideration to anticipate various threats, resulting in data leakage, misuse of information, modification, and data destruction. There are 36 public and private universities that utilize the academic information system provided by the software developed by Company XYZ. Limited resources in universities contribute to the weak handling of vulnerabilities in academic information systems. The research aims to determine the vulnerability level of academic information systems developed by Company XYZ through penetration testing. The research employs a deductive approach to explore academic system vulnerabilities based on incidents related to system security issues at a university. The research utilizes a combination of two testing methods: Penetration Testing Execution Standard (PTES) and Open Web Application Security Project (OWASP), chosen for their reliability, ease of use, and support by penetration testing tools. Penetration testing follows the PTES, involving seven steps: pre-engagement interaction, information collection, threat modeling, vulnerability analysis, exploitation, postexploitation, and reporting. The threat focus in the research aligns with the top 10 of 2021 OWASP, ranking the ten most critical security risks. Results reveal eight critical security issues based on measurements using the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) method. There are two high-level vulnerabilities, five medium-level vulnerabilities, and one low-level vulnerability. Moreover, the three principal vulnerabilities are Structured Query Language (SQL) Injection, broken access control, and weak encryption. Universities can enhance data integrity by independently remediating vulnerabilities discovered in the research. Furthermore, universities are encouraged to raise awareness within the academic community regarding the security of academic data.

Title: Understanding and Addressing Data Security and Privacy Concerns in Modern Cloud Computing Systems
Author: Ateeq, Ali; Alaghbari, Mohammed Abdulrazzaq; Ateeq, Ranyia Ali; Ahmed, Ammar Yousif
Abstract: This research examines the influence of the use of cloud computing on data management, with a specific emphasis on its ability to provide scalable solutions for storage and processing. The methodological approach involves doing a thorough assessment of existing literature and analyzing secondary data sources in order to provide a full overview of the topic matter. A systematic literature review was used to collect pertinent research results and data pertaining to the impact of cloud computing on data management. This approach facilitates the amalgamation of preexisting information and perspectives from many sources. The observations indicate that cloud computing has revolutionized data management by providing scalable and adaptable choices for both storage and processing. It has empowered enterprises to effectively manage substantial amounts of data and use computational resources as needed. Nevertheless, the ease and accessibility of cloud computing can give rise to difficulties in the confidentiality and protection of data. To address these difficulties, it is essential to implement encryption, and access control, and comply with data protection rules. The research concludes that cloud computing has fundamentally transformed data management, providing firms with robust tools to efficiently handle data. Nevertheless, it entails the need to employ resilient data privacy and security safeguards. Organizations should give priority to implementing measures such as encryption and access control in order to safeguard sensitive data. Adhering to legislation such as GDPR is crucial for maintaining trust and complying with legal obligations.

Author: Pande, S.D.; Khamparia, A.
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and its applications have risen to prominence as one of the most active study areas in recent years. In recent years, a rising number of AI applications have been applied in a variety of areas. Agriculture, transportation, medicine, and health are all being transformed by AI technology. The Internet of Things (IoT) market is thriving, having a significant impact on a wide variety of industries and applications, including e-health care, smart cities, smart transportation, and industrial engineering. Recent breakthroughs in artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques have reshaped various aspects of artificial vision, considerably improving the state of the art for artificial vision systems across a broad range of high-level tasks. As a result, several innovations and studies are being conducted to improve the performance and productivity of IoT devices across multiple industries using machine learning and artificial intelligence. Security is a primary consideration when analyzing the next generation communication network due to the rapid advancement of technology. Additionally, data analytics, deep intelligence, deep learning, cloud computing, and intelligent solutions are being employed in medical, agricultural, industrial, and health care systems that are based on the Internet of Things. This book will look at cutting-edge Network Attacks and Security solutions that employ intelligent data processing and Machine Learning (ML) methods. This book: Covers emerging technologies of network attacks and management aspects. Title: Soft Computing and Signal Processing, Proceedings of 6th ICSCSP 2023, Volume 1
Author: Sharma, Kulanshu; Rahul
Abstract: Blockchain technology is gaining importance because of its immutable distributed ledger and secure behavior. But still many industry applications are based on centralized servers which are risk-oriented. Meanwhile, maintaining vehicle registration records on pen and paper is very time consuming, and it also results in bribes (approaching brokers) to execute their work on priority. The data of vehicle registration in India is saved on the centralized server which may result in a single point of failure, data loss, and is also prone to unauthorized access by the users. This paper proposes an approach based on blockchain technology on distributed ledger and creates a web service which uses JSON Web Token to authenticate the users on the application and will allow only when the token gets authenticated. This system will assure no third parties involvement, no unauthorized user access, transparency, and increasing speed of registrations. Rest API’s are used which will interact with the web service, authenticate the user first, and then allow the user to access the blockchain.
